title: Design persistent native launch broker for sub-0.1s launches
description: Profiling for sandboxing-22uz showed Go-side startup repair planning is no longer the wall-clock limiter after batching ACL reads and adding a metadata-validated ACL health cache. Warm cached planning is ~0.25-1.07ms/op, but full native launch remains above the strict 0.1s target because per-launch sudo/helper invocation alone measured ~0.23-0.32s for installed helper usage checks, and profiled cached launches spent the remaining budget in run native command. Design and prove a persistent launch broker/service or equivalent architecture that preserves agent user isolation, sandbox_init enforcement, policy validation, fd isolation, metadata truthfulness, and repair semantics while avoiding sudo on every launch.
notes:
2026-06-15 post-rebuild default experimental profiling corrected the warm-broker evidence. After rebuilding checkout hazmat and hazmat-launch, cold broker startup measured 0.88s for ./hazmat --yes exec --no-backup --metadata-json -C /Users/dr/.codex/worktrees/68b1/hazmat -- /usr/bin/true with HAZMAT_EXPERIMENTAL_LAUNCH_BROKER=1. Warm samples mostly measured 0.09-0.10s but still spiked to 0.11-0.14s; built-in HAZMAT_SESSION_PREP_PROFILE attributed remaining variance to run native broker command with observed 0.03-0.16s. The split startup/child helper implementation remains useful and verified, but strict sub-0.1s is not yet proved. Added fallback temp-dir regression coverage and a comment-only TLA model note for helper-path split.

2026-06-15 profiling/cache follow-up: process-start profiling showed Go package/Cobra startup before session preparation is normally ~0.001-0.015s, so the remaining wall-clock spikes are not explained by Go init. Propagating HAZMAT_SESSION_PREP_PROFILE into broker child helpers exposed helper spans: helper sandbox_init is typically ~0.016-0.033s while helper argument/policy/session-dir setup rounds to ~0.000s. Pruning startup ACL cache retention reduced the live cache from 366 entries / ~109KB to the 7 current startup paths / ~1.4KB, preserving metadata-validated hits and converting unrelated entries into future cache misses. Gates passed: focused launch/session tests, GOTELEMETRY=off go test ./..., MC_SessionPermissionRepairs TLC (194,023 generated / 79,098 distinct / depth 7), and MC_LaunchFDIsolation TLC (1,312 generated / 928 distinct / depth 13). Conclusion: Zig rewrite of only Go launch control code is unlikely to buy the remaining gap; an alternative FD-safe lower-level or persistent host+agent launch path must avoid per-launch CLI/session planning and bound helper spawn/sandbox variance before it can plausibly prove <0.1s.

2026-06-15 forkserver proof: expanded MC_LaunchFDIsolation with an explicit broker child executor choice: current exec_helper vs future forkserver. The forkserver parent starts from the already-clean broker, retains only stdio plus a private socketpair-style control fd, and every forked launch child inherits then closes that control fd before policy open, sandbox_init, metadata, and final exec. Added ForkserverFDTableAllowlistedWhenReady and updated 09_launch_fd_isolation.md / VERIFIED.md / proof_ownership.tsv. TLC passed with 2,688 generated / 1,920 distinct / depth 15; focused Go ledger/import-boundary tests and git diff --check passed. This proves the safety boundary needed for a Zig/C forkserver or equivalent lower-level executor, which is the more promising optimization path than a one-shot Zig rewrite of the Go helper.

2026-06-15 implementation enabler: added HAZMAT_BROKER_CHILD_LAUNCH_HELPER as a broker-child-only helper override. This allows benchmarking a checkout/prototype Zig or C child helper without replacing the sudo-authorized startup helper used to cross into the agent broker. Focused helper/broker tests and GOTELEMETRY=off go test ./... passed.

2026-06-15 fast child helper experiment: added non-default hazmat-launch-fast C helper built with zig cc -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror for broker child profiling only. It mirrors the fd cleanup, policy path/owner/mode/deny-default validation, session temp creation, sandbox_init, metadata, direct exec, and shell exec boundary, and is listed under MC_LaunchFDIsolation governed code. Microbench exec mode: /usr/bin/true p50 ~9.9ms; Go hazmat-launch exec p50 ~18.6ms; fast helper exec p50 ~10.0ms. Real warm broker loop against ./hazmat --yes exec --no-backup --metadata-json -C repo -- /usr/bin/true: Go child helper p50 106.6ms / p90 149.3ms / p95 166.7ms / under100 19/50; fast child helper p50 84.9ms / p90 94.6ms / p95 94.9ms / under100 49/50, one 103.7ms outlier. Gates/smokes: make hazmat-launch-fast, hazmat-launch-fast exec /usr/bin/true, contained broker-child smoke with metadata, focused Go ledger/import-boundary test, git diff --check. Strict all-samples sub-0.1s is still not proved, but the lower-level child helper is materially better and supports continuing toward forkserver/default integration.

2026-06-15 profile propagation fix: default broker startup now carries HAZMAT_SESSION_PREP_PROFILE=yes through /usr/bin/env inside the agent-side hazmat-launch exec command, so broker child helpers can emit profile spans without manually starting a profiled broker. hazmat-launch-fast now emits helper spans; a clean warm profiled fast-helper launch showed host ACL snapshot 0.008s, prepare native policy ~0, run native broker command 0.030s, and helper sandbox_init 0.019s with other helper spans ~0. A separate noisy profiled run still showed run native broker command 0.680s, so strict tail latency remains unresolved. Gates: focused broker/profile tests, make hazmat-launch-fast, fast helper profile exec smoke, contained profiled broker-child smoke with helper spans, GOTELEMETRY=off go test ./..., git diff --check.
2026-06-16 cold-start target follow-up: after skipping Docker marker detection on the single-absolute-command exec fast path, rebuilt hazmat + hazmat-launch-fast and verified cold launches for ./hazmat/hazmat --yes exec --no-backup --metadata-json -C /Users/dr/.codex/worktrees/68b1/hazmat -- /usr/bin/true with HAZMAT_EXPERIMENTAL_LAUNCH_BROKER=1 and HAZMAT_BROKER_CHILD_LAUNCH_HELPER=/Users/dr/.codex/worktrees/68b1/hazmat/hazmat/hazmat-launch-fast. Final 20-sample broker-cold run, killing the broker before each sample, passed under the 1s cold target: min 204.4ms, p50 224.8ms, p75 265.8ms, p90 306.8ms, p95 393.8ms, max 401.8ms, mean 250.9ms, under1000 20/20. Default direct cold launch without the experimental broker also measured under target: 10/10 under 1s, p50 129.1ms, max 273.0ms. Earlier >1s samples correlated with stale CPU contention processes and high host load; after cleanup, broker-cold remained <0.5s even with high background load.
2026-06-16 nixpkgs cold-start follow-up: implemented two conservative cold-path optimizations. First, the experimental default launch broker now falls back to the already-proved direct helper path for the narrow single absolute-command fast path when no default broker is listening; explicit broker sockets remain fail-fast and non-fast scripts still start/retry the default broker. Second, added a healthy-only .git metadata health cache keyed by required/optional Git metadata path fingerprints; stale or missing fingerprints fall back to the existing fresh permission probe before planning/post-session repair. Profile evidence on /Users/dr/workspace/nixpkgs with a temp cache: first run git metadata permission detection 0.045s, second run 0.000s. Rebuilt hazmat and measured broker-absent launches with hazmat-launch-fast: 30 samples, first 181.6ms, p50 85.1ms, p90 129.3ms, p95 168.8ms, max 181.6ms, under1000 30/30. Gates passed: focused launch/Git preflight tests, go test ., MC_SessionPermissionRepairs TLC, MC_LaunchFDIsolation TLC, git diff --check.

title: Reduce minimal native launch below 0.1s
description: Critical follow-up to sandboxing-1bap: the minimal native contained command now verifies below 0.5s, but adoption-quality UX target is full launch under 0.1s for the same command: HAZMAT_LAUNCH_HELPER=/tmp/hazmat-launch-fast /tmp/hazmat-fast --yes exec --no-backup --metadata-json -C /Users/dr/.codex/worktrees/68b1/hazmat -- /usr/bin/true. Use profiling evidence before changing code. Preserve native seatbelt enforcement, policy validation, fd isolation, project write access, metadata truthfulness, explicit -R/-W grants, and explicit integration/GitHub/audit paths. Do not broaden the fast path beyond the same single-argument absolute exec shape without separate evidence and tests.
acceptance_criteria: Approved live timing demonstrates repeated real wall time below 0.1s for the same minimal command, with tests/benchmarks covering changed behavior; or remaining blocker is documented with measured evidence and the bead remains open.
notes: Added TLA-covered startup ACL observation optimization: batch ACL reads and metadata-validated ACL health cache for project/traverse repair planning. TLC MC_SessionPermissionRepairs passed after adding probe modes: 194,023 states generated, 79,098 distinct, depth 7. Focused tests and go test ./... pass. BenchmarkSessionPreparationPlainAbsoluteExecFastPath with warm temp ACL cache now measured ~0.25-1.07ms/op, down from ~10-18ms after batching and ~28-41ms before earlier optimizations. Full launch target is still not met on this host: profiled cached launch shows host ACL snapshot read ~0.001s, but run native command remains ~0.289s in one profile; installed helper non-interactive sudo usage checks measured ~0.23-0.32s just to invoke helper usage. Strict <0.1s now requires replacing per-launch sudo with a persistent launch broker/service or equivalent architecture, not more file scanning work.

title: Reduce native launch latency below 0.5s
description: Critical UX target: a minimal Hazmat native contained launch must complete under 0.5s without losing containment-critical behavior. Use profiling evidence to choose optimizations; Go, helper, or Zig/static-link changes are allowed only when they preserve the native seatbelt boundary, policy validation, fd isolation, project access controls, credential isolation, and launch metadata truthfulness. Start from current evidence: sandboxing-bjx9 measured real 3.37s, session preparation 1.8s, and planning host repairs 1.4s. Helper-only exec/fd cleanup was tens of milliseconds, so the first implementation target should be the Go-side planning path unless newer profiling contradicts it.
acceptance_criteria: Define the exact minimal launch command used for the target; profile enough phases to attribute remaining latency; implement scoped optimizations without removing critical containment functionality; targeted tests/benchmarks cover changed behavior; an approved live minimal native launch run demonstrates real wall time below 0.5s, or remaining blockers are filed with evidence and the P0 remains open.
notes:
2026-06-15 quiet exec UI optimization: plain native hazmat exec now launches with an empty sessionLaunchUI instead of starting the interactive status bar/alt-screen watcher path. Shell and harness launches keep their existing interactive UI behavior. Added TestExecLaunchUIDisablesInteractiveChrome; go test ./... passes.

2026-06-15 helper capability scan optimization: direct-exec compatibility detection now streams at most 2 MiB from the selected helper instead of os.ReadFile on the whole binary. A throwaway current helper build placed --hazmat-direct-exec at byte 837402 of a 5326690-byte binary, so the optimized path avoids scanning/allocating most of the helper while old/stale helpers still fall back to the shell path. Added reader boundary/limit tests; go test ./... passes.

2026-06-15 launch config skip optimization: plain native hazmat exec now skips loadConfig() during launch execution when sessionLaunchUI has no status bar or alt-screen watcher. Interactive shell/harness launches still load config so status_bar preferences apply. Added ApplyLaunchStatusBarConfig tests; go test ./... passes.

2026-06-15 Git repair lookup optimization: post-run .git metadata health checks now reuse a lazy gitAgentWriteProbe during one collectGitPermissionProblems pass, so agent UID and group membership lookups are cached while preserving the same ACL/mode checks and repair behavior. Added probe tests for no UID load on inheritable ACL checks and one group membership lookup for repeated same-GID files; go test ./... passes.

2026-06-15 runtime profiling expansion: HAZMAT_SESSION_PREP_PROFILE now breaks prepareSessionRuntime into agent temp, harness auth, Git HTTPS, optional Git SSH, and merge spans, and native launch execution records session runtime cleanup plus policy cleanup. This is intended to decide whether the next target is temp-dir lifecycle, Git HTTPS broker setup, helper/sudo handoff, or post-run repair. Focused profile tests and go test ./... pass. Full native timing still requires exact-command approval.

2026-06-15 Git HTTPS helper wrapper optimization: per-session Git HTTPS broker setup now injects credential.helper = !hazmat _git_https_credential <socket> directly instead of writing an executable wrapper file and exporting the socket path. This preserves helper reset and broker-backed get/store/erase behavior while removing one runtime file write from every Git-HTTPS-prepared session. Added inline helper runtime tests; go test ./... passes.

2026-06-15 helper-managed temp creation optimization: helpers advertising --hazmat-session-temp now create the already-policy-approved per-session TMPDIR inside the main hazmat-launch invocation, removing the separate pre-launch agentEnsureDir helper command while keeping stale-helper fallback and host-side cleanup. The new helper flag is constrained to /Users/agent/.cache/hazmat/tmp/<pid>-<n>, capability scanning still reads at most 2 MiB once per helper path, and MC_LaunchFDIsolation was updated/proved (640 generated, 448 distinct, depth 11) to preserve the fd table at sandbox_init. Focused launch tests and go test ./... pass.
2026-06-15 plain absolute exec integration fast path: single-argument absolute `hazmat exec` commands with no explicit integrations/GitHub/audit now skip automatic integration resolution and suggestion walking. This preserves explicit integrations and shell/toolchain exec forms with args, while avoiding project marker scans/probes for the minimal `/usr/bin/true` timing target. Focused tests and go test ./... pass.
2026-06-15 plain absolute exec advisory-scan fast path: the same single-argument absolute `hazmat exec` path now skips advisory repo setup discovery and Git safe.directory planning while retaining project ACL, launch-helper traversal, exposed-directory traversal, and Git metadata repair checks. Added focused tests plus BenchmarkSessionPreparationPlainAbsoluteExecFastPath. With HAZMAT_SESSION_PREP_PROFILE=yes and benchtime=1x, broad large-tree prep measured 960ms/op and the exact fast path measured 203ms/op, 846 allocs/op. go test ./... passes. Final live proof should set HAZMAT_LAUNCH_HELPER=/tmp/hazmat-launch-fast because /tmp/hazmat-fast otherwise selects the installed ~/.local helper, which is currently stale and lacks --hazmat-direct-exec/--hazmat-session-temp markers.
2026-06-15 runtime/access fast path and final proof: single-argument absolute `hazmat exec` now also skips ambient/default read grants, repo-local hook inspection, and the Git HTTPS credential broker runtime while preserving explicit -R/-W grants, project write access, native policy generation, sandbox_init, metadata JSON, project ACL/traverse/Git metadata repair checks, and explicit integration/GitHub/audit paths. BenchmarkSessionPreparationPlainAbsoluteExecFastPath with profiling measured 94.6ms/op and 523 allocs/op. go test ./... passes. Approved live timing with HAZMAT_LAUNCH_HELPER=/tmp/hazmat-launch-fast: profiled warm runs after the first cold run were 0.14s, 0.15s, 0.14s, 0.16s; unprofiled verification runs were 0.21s, 0.16s, 0.16s, 0.20s, 0.15s. Target <0.5s is demonstrated for the minimal command `/tmp/hazmat-fast --yes exec --no-backup --metadata-json -C /Users/dr/.codex/worktrees/68b1/hazmat -- /usr/bin/true` with the rebuilt helper override.
close_reason: Minimal native launch verified under 0.5s with profiling-backed fast paths and tests.

title: Build Hazmat runtime authority proof and test suite
description: Build the Hazmat-side regression suite for the runtime authority surfaces. This suite should run as ordinary project tests and cover pure adapters, capability declaration verification, conformance coverage, revocation states, hostbroker route facts, and trace emission.
acceptance_criteria:
- Golden fixture tests cover neutral authority preview and capability declaration bytes/hashes.
- Negative tests cover unsupported authority, weak isolation tier, missing conformance, stale revocation, wrong signer, wrong peer identity, and tampered trace hashes.
- Trace conformance fixtures are generated or exported for ops-side replay.
- The suite is documented in the issue closure notes with exact commands used.
notes: Dedicated test/proof closure gate for this epic.

title: Add Hazmat capability revocation and re-attestation checks
description: Add authoritative revocation and re-attestation checks for Hazmat runtime capabilities. The broker must be able to distinguish active, grace, stale, revoked, and reattestation-needed capability states without trusting cached declarations alone.
acceptance_criteria:
- Signed revocation feed coverage is explicit for Hazmat signer roots/backend families.
- Capability verification fails closed when required revocation coverage is absent or stale.
- active, grace, revoked, stale, and reattestation-needed states are represented and tested.
- New dispatch is denied for revoked/stale/reattestation-needed capabilities; grace requires the parent policy gate.
notes: Lifecycle verification surface.

title: Bind conformance evidence to Hazmat capability flags
description: Bind every declared-true Hazmat capability flag to positive conformance evidence. Evidence must point to checkable obligations or tests, not prose records, and must be scoped to the backend version and code revision named by the capability declaration.
acceptance_criteria:
- Coverage catalog entries name the capability flag, backend version, code revision, artifact hash, verifier identity, verifier result hash, and obligation/test name.
- Capability verification fails when any declared-true flag lacks matching coverage.
- Negative tests cover wrong artifact hash, wrong invariant/test name, mismatched backend version, stale verifier result, and missing verifier signature.
- Existing Hazmat TLA/test artifacts are referenced by content hash where available.
notes: Proof/conformance surface for SR1/SR2-style trust anchors.

title: Implement signed runtime.capability.v1 declaration emitter
description: Implement a Hazmat-owned runtime.capability.v1 declaration emitter for macOS containment backends. The declaration is an authority-bearing artifact and must be signed, content-hashed, validity-bounded, and scoped to a backend version/code revision.
acceptance_criteria:
- Capability declarations are signed by the configured Hazmat capability signer.
- Declarations include backend_version, backend_code_revision, isolation_tier, attestation_tier, valid_from, valid_until, reattest_after, capability_set_fingerprint, and revocation feed reference.
- Unsigned, expired, future-dated, wrong-signer, wrong-version, and tampered declarations are rejected in tests.
- No boolean can_* flag is treated as sufficient without isolation tier and conformance metadata.
notes: Implementation + verification gate for later ops dispatch.

title: Add Hazmat fixture adapter for neutral runtime authority preview
description: Add a Hazmat-side adapter that consumes the neutral runtime.authority.v1 fixtures and produces a macOS containment/session preview. The preview must be pure and side-effect free: path grants, credential mode, network posture, session home, logical resource labels, and requested isolation tier are rendered for inspection but do not launch a session.
acceptance_criteria:
- Valid neutral fixtures produce deterministic preview output.
- Invalid or unknown authority fields fail closed with inspectable errors.
- Preview output identifies unsupported fields instead of silently dropping them.
- Unit tests cover path grants, network-denied mode, empty-home semantics, credential-broker-required mode, logical resources, and malformed inputs.
notes: Implementation surface; no runtime launch or credential access.
close_reason: Implemented side-effect-free runtime.authority.v1 preview adapter with deterministic output, fail-closed parsing, unsupported-field reporting, and Go test/vet coverage.

title: Project-comms runtime authority support for Hazmat
description: Implement the Hazmat-owned runtime authority surfaces required by the autonomous ops triage and project communication roadmap. Hazmat is the local macOS containment authority: it must compile neutral runtime authority into a previewable containment/session contract, emit signed capability declarations, bind those declarations to positive conformance evidence, expose host-derived route facts for local intake, and emit traces for conformance replay. This epic must not grant new execution authority by itself; ops dispatch remains gated by the parent broker.
acceptance_criteria:
- Hazmat consumes neutral runtime-authority fixtures and produces preview artifacts without executing jobs.
- Signed runtime.capability.v1 declarations include backend version, backend code revision, isolation tier, validity, re-attestation cadence, revocation feed reference, capability-set fingerprint, and signer identity.
- Every declared-true capability has checkable conformance coverage and fails closed when coverage, verifier result, revocation, or validity checks are missing or stale.
- Hostbroker route facts are derived from observed launch/session facts, not requester-authored payload fields.
- Trace events are sufficient for ops-side trace conformance and contain hashes/ids, not secret values.

title: Build deterministic credential sync regression harness
description: Add a test harness for credential sync regressions that does not depend on live OAuth refresh. title: [library] Per-session broker socket API: request-content protocol + lifecycle
description:
Library-first Model B transport (authority logic is .4). Expose a reusable per-session broker socket API that the contained agent uses to submit CLOSED request payloads: bounded request CONTENT only, never authority fields.

Lifecycle: created/activated ONLY after confirmed sandbox_init [P1b]; reachable by the contained agent but never exposing key/registry/ledger; mirror the Git-SSH transport broker shape (ephemeral path, 0o660 host+agent where appropriate, removed on session exit), but keep the implementation reusable rather than Beadpost-CLI-specific. The socket layer hands payloads to the .4 broker API, which DERIVES project/session/tier from launch facts and ignores agent-supplied authority fields.

This is socket protocol + lifecycle, NOT token-file plumbing and NOT an executable-level Beadpost integration: [P2a] no agent-readable token and no key path in the agent context, so the agent-owned 0700 temp-dir problem is gone. Define the bounded request-payload schema, framing, error/teardown semantics, and library interfaces needed by Beadpost or other future consumers.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable per-session socket API is created/activated only after confirmed sandbox_init and is removed on session exit. The contained agent can submit only bounded request-content payloads over the socket. The socket handler passes content to the host broker API, which derives all authority from launch facts. The agent cannot read or infer the key, token, registry, ledger, --attestation-key path, or any host-authority path through this transport. The implementation does not bake in Beadpost CLI execution as the transport contract.

title: [library] Host broker API: mint/verify attestation + call Beadpost API
description:

After confirmed sandbox_init [P1b], the broker API:
(1) MINTS a beadpost.containment.attestation.v1 token from LAUNCH FACTS only - canonical pathpolicy.ProjectRoot (Abs+EvalSymlinks+Clean) matching Beadpost NormalizeProjectPath, agent uid (default 599 == BEADPOST_AGENT_UID), effective-posture tier (.5), issued_at/expires_at RFC3339Nano UTC short TTL, crypto/rand nonce; byte-exact HMAC-SHA256 over canonical JSON; bound to the per-request fingerprint [P1c].
(2) VERIFIES it host-side.
(3) Calls Beadpost delivery/review package APIs host-side, with Beadpost key/registry/ledger kept host-side.

Hazmat has zero crypto today. The key is loaded only inside the broker (dr) through the .3 key-custody API; NO agent-readable token and NO key path in the agent context. The token is the internal contract artifact between the Hazmat broker and the Beadpost membrane. Never trust agent-supplied authority fields.

If Beadpost currently hides the needed delivery/review logic under internal packages, coordinate a Beadpost-side API extraction instead of hard-coding process execution as the architecture.

title: [library] Host-authority key custody API + pathpolicy deny
description:

If an operator command is added, it must be a thin wrapper over the library API. If anyone proposes putting this key into hazmat init/rollback or rollback cleanup, stop and update MC_SetupRollback first; that is a separate design decision, not this bead.

title: [decision] Model B: contained-agent submitter + dr-owned host broker
description:
Decision record for the Hazmat-Beadpost invocation model. The selected model is Model B, renamed for precision: contained-agent submitter + dr-owned host broker.

Confirmed against code: beadpost deliver --security-boundary reads both the HMAC key (internal/broker/attestation.go:90) and the token (:94) in one process, resolves the project from cwd, and verifies the UID encoded in the token via expectedAgentUID(opts). It does not check the running process UID; only onboard doctor checks os.Getuid (onboard.go:421).

Consequences: the contained agent must not run Beadpost delivery because it cannot read the dr-owned key. The contained agent only submits bounded request content. The dr-owned host broker holds the key/registry/ledger, derives authority from confirmed launch facts, binds the request, and invokes Beadpost host-side.

The old design tuple (dr-side signing + agent-readable token + Beadpost reading token/key in the same process) is rejected as incoherent.
design:
Selected model: contained-agent submitter + dr-owned host broker.

The contained agent connects to a per-session socket created only after confirmed sandbox_init and sends request-content payloads only. The dr-owned broker derives project/session/tier/uid/fingerprint authority from launch facts and effective posture; it never accepts authority fields from the agent. The broker mints/uses a request-bound beadpost.containment.attestation.v1 token host-side, keeps Beadpost key/registry/ledger host-side, and invokes Beadpost delivery/review host-side.

Rejected alternatives:
- Host-only scan of draft beads was not chosen because request/session provenance is awkward and easier to get wrong.
- Contained-side Beadpost delivery was rejected because deliver reads the HMAC key in-process.
- Agent-visible bearer token custody was rejected because the selected broker model does not need it and it creates avoidable replay/custody risk.
acceptance_criteria: Closed decision records Model B with rationale; specifies confirmed sandbox_init before broker/mint, per-request provenance binding, host-side verifier/key co-location, no agent-readable token, and no key path in the agent context. Implementation beads .4/.6 are scoped to host broker authority logic and per-session request-content socket respectively.
notes: Final terminology: contained-agent submitter + dr-owned host broker. The agent submits bounded request content; the broker derives authority from launch facts and invokes Beadpost host-side. Avoid shorthand that implies Beadpost delivery runs inside the contained agent.
close_reason: Closed

title: [epic] Hazmat-Beadpost library-first contained-agent host broker
description:
Build Model B as a library-first architecture: a contained-agent submitter plus dr-owned host broker primitives that Beadpost can compose. Hazmat proves confirmed launch context and per-request provenance; Beadpost governs disclosure/task transfer.

Policy: do not implement this as a Hazmat executable-level Beadpost integration. Hazmat should expose reusable Go package APIs for host-authority path denial, key custody, launch-fact/effective-posture authority derivation, per-session socket lifecycle, and request-content-only broker submission. Hazmat CLI/config commands may exist only as thin operator UX over those APIs.

The contained agent submits bounded, closed request-content payloads over a per-session broker socket. The dr-owned broker starts only after confirmed sandbox_init, derives project/session/tier from launch facts, holds the HMAC key plus Beadpost registry/ledger host-side, mints/uses beadpost.containment.attestation.v1 as an internal request-bound contract artifact, and invokes Beadpost delivery/review through a package/API boundary rather than shelling out as the primary integration model.

No agent-readable attestation token exists. No attestation key path exists in the agent context. The agent never supplies authority fields; the broker ignores anything authority-shaped in submitted content and derives authority from launch facts only.

Honest threat model: on a single shared host with a shared symmetric HMAC key, this defends against the contained agent forging or widening cross-project authority. A dr/host-root attacker can forge and remains trusted/out of scope.
design:
Final model: contained-agent submitter + dr-owned host broker, library-first.

Library-first policy:
1. Hazmat exports containment/broker primitives as public Go packages.
2. Beadpost exposes/refactors delivery/review logic as a package API Hazmat can call.
3. Hazmat CLI/config commands are optional thin wrappers, not the integration boundary.
4. No Go implementation bead should add Beadpost-specific persistent state to hazmat init/rollback unless MC_SetupRollback is updated first and the policy is explicitly revisited.
5. No broker implementation should rely on CLI shell-out as the steady-state architecture; CLI may be used only as a temporary compatibility shim if captured as follow-up debt.

Authority flow:
1. hazmat-launch confirms sandbox_init succeeded.
2. Hazmat activates a per-session dr-owned broker socket reachable by the contained agent.
3. The agent submits request content only; project/session/tier/uid/fingerprint authority is never accepted from the agent.
4. The host broker derives authority from launch facts and effective posture, mints a request-bound beadpost.containment.attestation.v1 token host-side, verifies/fails closed host-side, and calls Beadpost delivery/review APIs with key/registry/ledger kept outside the agent.
5. The socket tears down on session exit.

Spec-first split:
- MC_SeatbeltPolicy proves the attestation key deny floor.
- MC_LaunchFDIsolation proves confirmed-containment mint/broker ordering and no authority fd reaches the agent.
- MC_BeadpostBrokerBoundary proves the request membrane and no cross-session/cross-authority confusion.

Out of scope: making Hazmat a workflow-specific Beadpost CLI wrapper, making Beadpost a containment system, or treating the HMAC token as non-repudiation against dr/root.
acceptance_criteria: All three TLA spec beads (.2/.9/.10) pass their targeted TLC checks and ownership/roster hygiene; implementation beads remain blocked until then. The implemented broker keeps key/registry/ledger host-side, exposes only a per-session request-content socket to the agent, derives authority from launch facts/effective posture, binds authority per request, invokes Beadpost through a package/API boundary, and documents the shared-host HMAC threat model and Beadpost UID semantics. Hazmat command surfaces, if any, are wrappers over reusable library APIs rather than the integration boundary.
notes: PAUSE POINT (2026-06-09): .3 (738bfba) and .5 (1861ab2) done + committed on branch beadpost-attestation-specs; spec phase be09aff. Per decision, Hazmat broker implementation PAUSES at .4 until Beadpost bp-fyg.6 (delivery/review package/API surface) exists. No CLI shim for .4 unless that debt is explicitly reopened. Remaining: .4 (blocked on .5[done]+bp-fyg.6), .6 (needs .4), .7 (needs .4+.6), .8 docs.

title: Gate trace behind strict debug build
description: Before merging trace work, make hazmat trace developer-only: exclude it from default/release builds, require an explicit debug build tag, and fail/debug-configure before compilation when required trace dependencies are unavailable. Runtime trace should not silently degrade or launch a partial trace.
design: Architecture: make trace a developer-only debug surface. Default package builds compile a no-op debug command registrar, so release binaries have no trace subcommand and do not compile trace implementation files. Debug builds opt in with the hazmat_debug build tag; only then does the registrar attach hazmat trace to the run command group. All trace implementation and tests carry hazmat_debug build constraints, with platform files constrained as hazmat_debug && darwin, hazmat_debug && linux, or hazmat_debug && !darwin && !linux. Add a configure-debug-trace script/Make target that developers run before compiling a debug binary; it checks required host tools for the target platform and fails before go build if anything is missing. Runtime trace remains strict too: backend preflight runs before bundle creation and launch, and observer startup returns errors instead of trace-errors.log degradation. Linux requires strace, ps, ls/stat, journalctl, dmesg, /proc, and readable capability/status metadata. macOS requires sudo -n readiness plus dtruss, fs_usage, opensnoop, log, script, ps/ls/uname/sw_vers/csrutil. Remove no-syscalls/no-transcript escape hatches from the debug CLI so trace always means full trace.
acceptance_criteria: Default and release builds do not contain the trace command or trace implementation; debug developers build with -tags hazmat_debug after a configure/prerequisite step; trace preflights all required observer dependencies and refuses to launch when any required trace capability is absent; normal check-fast and release builds pass without trace; debug-tagged tests/gates cover trace command registration and strict dependency behavior.
close_reason: Completed: trace is gated behind hazmat_debug with generated configure marker, strict dependency preflight, release/default command omission, Linux Docker strict smoke, docs and gates.

title: Codex desktop sandboxing via contained app-server
description: Build the practical sandboxing path for Codex desktop usage by making Hazmat own the execution backend first. The preferred architecture is a Hazmat-contained Codex app-server running as the agent user under native SBPL, user isolation, credential materialization, and network policy, with the stock desktop app attaching only if that can be proven to keep filesystem, process, browser, and shell side effects on the contained backend. Full GUI containment remains a stretch item after the backend path is reliable.
design:
Implementation plan:
1. Keep the stock Codex desktop app out of the first implementation path. Do not launch, quit, kill, or mutate the host app during backend harness work.
2. Turn the current pass-through app-server prototype into an explicit managed backend mode when needed: lifecycle, stdio or Unix socket transport, socket directory permissions, startup readiness, teardown, and clear stderr/stdout protocol boundaries.
3. Validate every app-server side-effect surface against Hazmat outer containment: command/exec, process/spawn, fs/readFile, fs/writeFile, fs/remove, thread/shellCommand, browser-use or app-specific subprocesses, credential paths, host state paths, and network none.
4. Probe whether the stock Codex desktop app can attach to a Hazmat-owned app-server or remote environment without falling back to a host-user local app-server for any side-effect API.
5. Classify Codex App host-state paths before granting or denying any app-specific Library, cache, socket, sqlite, browser-use, or .codex state.
6. If any verified area changes, update the relevant TLA+ model and design note before implementation, then run TLC before code changes.

Autonomous testing plan:
1. Prefer tests that spawn a short-lived Hazmat-owned app-server with scratch project paths and fake probe credentials, never the live desktop app.
2. Provide a single non-interactive smoke command that validates initialize, command execution, project file access, credential denial, host-state denial where applicable, and network-none behavior.
3. Add unit tests for argument routing, protocol-clean stdout, status UI suppression, socket path permissions, and policy generation.
4. Add regression coverage for app-server APIs that bypass Codex inner sandboxing but should still be constrained by Hazmat outer containment.
5. Make gate integration opt-in or prerequisite-aware until CI has the necessary agent account, Codex binary, sudo rule, and macOS seatbelt support.
6. Every test must clean up subprocesses, temp projects, fake credentials, sockets, and app-server state.
acceptance_criteria: The epic is complete when Hazmat has a documented and tested contained Codex app-server backend path; autonomous smoke/regression tests can run without touching the users live Codex desktop app; filesystem/process/network side-effect surfaces are covered or explicitly documented as residual risk; desktop attach feasibility is documented; host-state deny decisions are recorded; and any policy/model changes required by verified areas have passed TLC and normal Go/pre-push gates.
notes: Blocked on explicit approval for Codex desktop attach live smoke. Exact command after quitting Codex App: scripts/check-codex-desktop-attach-smoke.sh --run --i-understand-this-may-launch-codex-app

title: Probe Codex App external app-server attach path
description: Determine whether the stock Codex desktop app can attach to an externally launched app-server, app-server daemon, or remote execution environment that Hazmat owns. The research question is whether the GUI can remain host-side while all shell/filesystem/tool execution is routed to a Hazmat-contained backend instead of the app local host-user app-server.
acceptance_criteria: The result documents whether current Codex App can select or enroll an external app-server, app-server daemon, or remote environment; if yes, the accepted transport/configuration and residual host-side surfaces are documented; if no, the missing upstream capability is stated clearly. The current stock desktop app does not expose a documented arbitrary unix/ws external app-server endpoint; it starts a resolved Codex CLI with app-server args for the standard local transport. Static bundle evidence shows CODEX_CLI_PATH and SSH codex_cli_command are plausible command-substitution routes into a Hazmat-managed stdio app-server backend. Residual host GUI/auth/cache/keychain surfaces and browser/computer-use placement are documented in docs/research/2026-05-28-codex-ui-app-sandboxing.md. title: codex: arrow keys don't navigate first-run auth picker under hazmat
description:
Inside 'hazmat codex' the codex first-run auth picker (Sign in with ChatGPT / Device Code / API key) renders correctly but does NOT respond to Up/Down arrow navigation. Confirmed reproducer: fresh 'hazmat codex' launch on a clean codex install with no pre-typed input, on macOS Tahoe terminal.

Discriminators verified:
  - codex outside hazmat: arrow keys WORK on the same auth screen
  - 'hazmat claude --resume' picker: arrow keys WORK (when not pre-typed during hazmat loading)
So this is hazmat-specific AND codex-specific within hazmat.

Working theory areas (not yet root-caused):
  - Status bar interactions with terminal modes: scroll-region set via \033[1;%dr at hazmat/statusbar.go:108 + TIOCSWINSZ shrinking reported rows by 1 at hazmat/statusbar.go:127-130. Both could trigger SIGWINCH or terminal-mode flushes that crossterm/ratatui handles differently than claude's Ink.
  - Application cursor mode (DECCKM): crossterm enables it for TUI apps; arrows then send ESC O A/B/C/D instead of ESC [ A/B/C/D. Something in hazmat's launch path may be intercepting or stripping DECCKM enable.
  - hazmat-launch fd handling: closes 3+, keeps 0/1/2 (verified). Process group / controlling tty status under sudo -> hazmat-launch chain not yet inspected.

Workaround that exists today: 'hazmat config import codex' (landed in f5a85b7) copies host auth.json into the agent home so codex launches authed and never shows this picker.
acceptance_criteria: 'hazmat codex' on a fresh codex install (no auth.json) responds to Up/Down arrow keys to move the > marker between options 1/2/3 in the auth picker, matching the host-only codex behavior. Verified by visual confirmation in macOS terminal.

title: Refactor self-hosting and integration-check code for maintainable stack waves

Use the resulting source state as the foundation for repo-matrix validation. Focus on removing one-off shell coupling, clarifying reusable test helpers and runner structure, and separating self-hosting checks from cross-repo stack checks before adding the wave-based external corpus.

Post-bootstrap hardening lane: before stack-wave work, resolve session-permission audit/proof/docs gaps tracked in sandboxing-4c2, sandboxing-hip, sandboxing-4xb, sandboxing-sbb, and sandboxing-3ks. Keep repo-matrix implementation blocked behind this lane.
Preferred refactor direction: make session setup plan-driven. Introduce a typed SessionPlan that contains access, snapshot, launch, and host-mutation subplans. Both hazmat explain and real session launch should consume the same plan so preview and execution cannot drift. Model every host-side permission change as a declared MutationOp with fields such as reason, target paths, persistence, consent surface, rollback/manual-repair story, and proof_scope (for example: modeled-by-TLA vs tests/docs only). Keep resolvers pure where possible; only the mutation executor may apply host changes.
close_reason: Completed the post-bootstrap refactor lane: session setup now plans and renders host mutations explicitly, which is the new base for stack-wave work.

title: Align integration resolution with toolchains actually reachable inside contained sessions
description:
Autonomous QA on master found runtime mismatches between the integration contract and the binaries actually available inside hazmat exec sessions. Go case: hazmat exec -C /Users/dr/workspace/beads --docker=none --integration go --no-backup -- sh -lc 'printf "GOROOT=%s
" ""; command -v go || true; printf "READ=%s
" ""' produced GOROOT=/opt/homebrew/Cellar/go/1.26.1/libexec and READ=[/opt/homebrew/Cellar/go/1.26.1/libexec], but command -v go printed nothing. Rust case: hazmat exec -C /Users/dr/workspace/poly --integration rust --no-backup -- sh -lc 'command -v rustc || true; rustc --print sysroot 2>/dev/null || true; printf "READ=%s

title: Scope decision: shared-daemon Docker is unsupported in containment
description: Hazmat's security model treats host Docker daemon access as categorically incompatible with containment (session.go:869, threat-matrix.md:87, tier3-docker-sandboxes.md:261). Projects that depend on the shared host daemon (external Docker networks, Traefik labels, scripts booting other Compose projects) cannot use Tier 3 (private daemon is the wrong Docker world) and cannot use Docker in Tier 2 (socket is 0700). This is the correct security position. The issue is that hazmat's current UX does not acknowledge this class of project — it either misroutes to Tier 3 or blocks with messaging that implies Tier 3 is the happy path. This issue records the scope decision: shared-daemon Docker is explicitly unsupported for containment. The CLI and docs should say so clearly. Future work may add a broker/proxy mode, but that is a separate security model, not a patch on Tier 2 or 3.
design: Invariant preserved: never share the host Docker socket. Shared-daemon projects get code-only sessions with clear messaging. Private-daemon projects continue routing to Tier 3. The flag space is --docker=auto|none|sandbox. Persistent per-project config stored in host config via dedicated subcommand.
notes: Evidence: session.go:869-871 (code comment), threat-matrix.md:87 (Tier 2 intentionally excludes Docker), tier3-docker-sandboxes.md:261 (categorical rule). Real-world case: niche-sieve depends on shared host daemon via docker-compose.dev.yml external proxy network and dev-up.sh booting docker-infra Traefik.
close_reason: Scope decision made: shared-daemon Docker is explicitly unsupported for containment. The security model (session.go:869, threat-matrix.md:87, tier3-docker-sandboxes.md:261) treats host daemon access as categorically incompatible with containment. v1 is clear unsupported-project handling with code-only session workflow, not safe shared-daemon mode. Implementation tracked in sandboxing-pi5 (CLI/config), sandboxing-m0o (detection/messaging), sandboxing-yfd (docs).

The epic covers the safe path from design to execution: update research docs, prove Apple Container launch containment, add a plan-only backend compiler, spike host behavior on macOS 26 Apple silicon, then implement a narrow experimental runtime only after the blocking proof and probe work is done. Scope is Apple container/container machine support as specified in docs/plans/2026-06-10-apple-container-backend-design.md; Docker Sandbox and native macOS containment remain separate backends.
design: Phase order: (0) refresh research docs, (1) TLA/model launch containment, (2) plan-only compiler and metadata, (3) host behavior spike, (4) experimental runtime. The runtime task stays blocked on model, compiler, and spike; container machine and network allowlists remain future work unless separately modeled.
acceptance_criteria: Epic is done when the research docs are current, the Apple Container launch containment model is proved, the plan-only backend compiler and explain surface exist, host behavior probes are recorded, and an experimental apple-container runtime is implemented behind an explicit gate with gated macOS 26 smoke coverage.
notes: Progress 2026-06-10 (branch apple-container-backend, pushed through 90ea2a5): 4/5 children done — x4za (model proved), 7q3u (docs), x2ca (plan-only compiler + explain), ajmn (host spike on container 1.0.0). Remaining: ifkc, BLOCKED on identity-model decision — spike F1 shows CLI-as-agent fails on 1.0.0 (per-user-session apiserver). Decision needed: invoking-user CLI (weaker host boundary, design revision) vs wait for upstream vs stay plan-only.
close_reason: All acceptance criteria met (branch apple-container-backend, pushed through bda4b8e): research docs current at container 1.0.0 GA (7q3u); MC_AppleContainerLaunch proved, 134,720 states, promoted into the suite (x4za); plan-only compiler + hazmat explain --backend=apple-container with capability gaps (x2ca); host behavior probes recorded with design-impacting F1 finding and probe harness committed (ajmn); experimental apple-container runtime behind HAZMAT_EXPERIMENTAL_APPLE_CONTAINER=1, exec-only, with gated macOS 26 smoke coverage green on real container 1.0.0 (ifkc). Identity model revised to invoking-user with blunt contract per dr's Option 1 decision. Future work not in scope: network-none support (model extension), network allowlist profiles, container machine mode, harness images.

title: Implement experimental Apple Container runtime
description: After the Apple Container launch model, plan-only compiler, and host behavior spike are complete, implement internal/runtime/applecontainer behind an explicit experimental gate. Support a narrow hazmat exec path first, network default only, explicit images, session-scoped credential delivery, named container lifecycle, and gated macOS 26 smoke tests.
notes: DECISION (dr, 2026-06-10): Option 1 — run the container CLI as the invoking user with blunt contract wording. Constraints: experimental gate; contract says 'Host identity: invoking user'; no native-parity claims; strict mount planning preserved (no home, no credential parents, no sockets/SSH/env inheritance); always --user (no guest root); network default only (none requires model/compiler update first); hazmat exec only; design doc Identity Model revised before runtime code lands. Positioning: 'Linux VM-per-session execution with Hazmat-planned host mounts. Host file IO occurs as the invoking macOS user. Host account isolation is not provided by this backend.'
close_reason: Experimental runtime shipped under Option 1 (invoking-user identity, blunt contract). All constraints met: HAZMAT_EXPERIMENTAL_APPLE_CONTAINER=1 gate; contract prints 'Host identity: invoking user (host account isolation NOT provided)'; no parity claims; strict mount planning preserved (typed deny-zone validation, no home/credential/socket/SSH/env); always non-root --user (invoking uid/gid); network default only, none/allowlists fail closed; exec-only (claude test-enforced flag-free); design doc Identity Model revised before runtime code; MC_AppleContainerLaunch re-run green. Gated smoke tests green on macOS 26.5 / container 1.0.0: mount r/w, non-root guest, deny zones invisible, exit codes, residue-free cleanup.

title: Spike Apple Container host behavior for Hazmat
description: On macOS 26 Apple silicon with apple/container installed, measure the behavior Hazmat depends on before runtime implementation: running container as the macOS agent user, bind-mount ownership and write semantics, numeric UID/GID behavior, container system status/version JSON, internal network and host gateway reachability, cleanup of named containers, and whether any true no-network mode exists.
notes:
BLOCKED on human action: host is eligible (macOS 26.5, Apple silicon) but apple/container is not installed and Hazmat must never install it (admin authority, per design doc Host Admission). Probe harness is ready: scripts/spike-apple-container.sh (commit f4f6d75 on apple-container-backend). To unblock: install apple/container >= 1.0.0 from https://github.com/apple/container/releases, run 'container system start', then 'sh scripts/spike-apple-container.sh' and record results in this bead + design-doc open questions.
Apple Container installed and spike executed on 2026-06-10. Host: macOS 26.5 arm64. container/container-apiserver 1.0.0 commit ee848e3, system status running for invoking user. Results saved at spike-apple-container-results/spike-20260610-151108.md. Key findings: (1) sudo -u agent whoami works, but sudo -u agent container system status reports not running and sudo -u agent container ls fails unauthorized request, so runtime cannot assume agent-user CLI access yet. (2) Bind mounts are readable/writable from root guest; guest-created files map to host uid 501 gid 0 when CLI runs as invoking user. (3) --user 502:20 changes guest-visible uid/gid but host-side ownership still maps to uid 501 gid 0 in this probe. (4) internal network is hostOnly with gateway 192.168.128.1; probe saw no external egress to 1.1.1.1:443 and no SSH on gateway:22, but host gateway semantics still need careful runtime treatment. (5) cleanup by exact container name worked; no spike containers or volumes remained. (6) --network none produced loopback-only interface and no egress to 1.1.1.1:443 in this probe. (7) --no-dns on internal network blocked DNS resolution.
close_reason: Spike completed on macOS 26.5 / apple-container 1.0.0 (docs/research/2026-06-10-apple-container-spike.md, commit 90ea2a5). All listed measurements done: agent-user CLI execution FAILS (per-user-session apiserver, unauthorized request — design-impacting F1); VirtioFS host IO runs as CLI-invoking user regardless of guest UID (F2); --network none exists, loopback-only (F3); host 0.0.0.0 services reachable from default AND internal networks (F4, #719 confirmed); exact-name cleanup residue-free (F5); status/version JSON shapes recorded (F6).

title: [docs] Document library-first Hazmat<->Beadpost attestation contract
description:
Add docs describing the final library-first Model B contract: contained-agent submitter + dr-owned host broker primitives that Beadpost composes. The contract surface is the per-session request-content socket plus the broker internal request-bound beadpost.containment.attestation.v1 artifact; no token file or attestation key path is ever agent-visible.

Make the policy explicit: Hazmat should expose reusable containment/broker APIs, not a workflow-specific executable-level Beadpost integration. Hazmat CLI/config commands, if added, are thin operator UX over those APIs. Beadpost delivery/review should be reached through package/API boundaries; any temporary CLI shell-out must be documented as compatibility debt, not architecture.

Cover key custody (explicit host-authority library API, dr-owned, pathpolicy deny, agent-denied), confirmed-containment broker activation, effective-posture tier mapping, per-request provenance/fingerprint binding, socket lifecycle, Beadpost host-side delivery/review API invocation, and the honest single-host/shared-key threat model. State the sharp reuse boundary: Hazmat proves launch context and request provenance; Beadpost governs disclosure/task transfer; neither becomes a CLI wrapper for the other.

Cross-link/update Beadpost docs to replace manual beadpost attest create guidance with the Hazmat broker/library flow where appropriate. Include Beadpost-side follow-ups: nonce/replay ledger, explicit strong tier, request binding, optional host binding, deliver UID semantics, and package API extraction if Beadpost internals still block library composition.
acceptance_criteria: Docs cover Model B contract/custody/tier/provenance/socket lifecycle/threat model and the library-first policy; explicitly state no agent-readable token and no key path in agent context; Hazmat APIs are documented as reusable primitives; Beadpost README/operations guidance distinguishes host-side API delivery from contained-agent submission; deliver UID semantics are documented as token-encoded UID, not live process UID; Beadpost-side follow-ups including package API extraction are cross-linked.

title: Make Claude session export preserve Workflow artifacts across host resume
description:
When a Claude Code session that ran inside Hazmat is exported with `hazmat export claude session` and then continued outside containment with host Claude (`claude --resume "$(hazmat export claude session)" --fork-session`), dynamic Workflow/subagent artifacts can still point at the original agent-owned session store under `/Users/agent/.claude/projects/...`.

Observed log from an exported kee-ios session: after a long Claude Workflow run completed most agents and crashed in a late non-parallel StructuredOutput step, the host-side resumed Claude tried to inspect `/Users/agent/.claude/projects/-Users-dr-workspace-kee-ios/<session-id>/subagents/workflows/wf_*` and failed with `permission denied`. Claude then reasoned that the Workflow runtime could resume by run ID, but the transcript shows cache/artifact handling became confused: expensive baseline/review/synthesis agents were assumed cached, while critique/finalize had to be rerun with different output shape.

Current code path: `exportClaudeSession` selects the agent project dir, stages a bundle, installs it into the invoker Claude project dir, and rewrites only `sessions-index.json` fullPath metadata (`hazmat/export.go`). `agentClaudeBundleManifest` copies the transcript, `sessions-index.json`, and every regular file/directory under the same-named session sidecar dir. `copyAgentClaudeFile` reads each file as the agent and writes a new host-owned 0600 copy. This fixes ownership for copied files, but it does not rebase opaque sidecar metadata, transcript tool outputs, Workflow journals, or cache manifests that may contain absolute `/Users/agent/.claude/projects/...` paths.

This is not the general Claude import boundary. It is an export/resume correctness issue for per-session runtime artifacts that the export command already claims to copy. The desired behavior should be explicit and clean: either exported Workflow artifacts remain usable by host Claude after resume, or volatile/unportable artifacts are deliberately omitted/invalidated with documented behavior. The current middle state is bad because artifacts are copied but still lead host Claude toward inaccessible agent-home paths and unreliable cache expectations.
design:
Investigate the actual Claude Code sidecar layout for Workflow/subagent artifacts under `<session-id>/subagents/workflows/`, especially journal/cache files that contain absolute paths or run IDs. Confirm whether the relevant paths are stored in transcript JSONL, sidecar JSON, workflow journals, cache manifests, or all of the above.

Preferred direction to evaluate first: preserve path validity through controlled permissions instead of blindly copying and rebasing a large opaque artifact tree. Options may include making only the specific exported agent project/session sidecar tree host-readable/traversable via the existing agent helper/group model, creating host-side references that leave original absolute paths usable, or running a targeted permission repair at export time. This must not expose agent credentials, global `.claude` config, other projects, or broad `/Users/agent` state to the host Claude process.

Fallback direction if live agent-path access is not acceptable: implement a narrow rebasing/normalization pass for known portable Workflow artifact files and transcript/index fields. Avoid broad string replacement unless the file formats are understood enough to make it safe. If some artifact classes are volatile by design, exclude them from export and document that Workflow cache resume does not survive the handoff.

Check TLA+ governance before changing setup/init, persistent permission repair, credential/session permission policy, or seatbelt-relevant agent-home sharing. `hazmat/init.go` step changes or persistent permission mutations in verified areas require model/design-note work first.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Reproduce the failure with a contained Claude session that creates Workflow/subagent artifacts, export it, resume with host Claude, and verify where stale `/Users/agent/.claude/projects/...` references are consumed.
2. Decide and document the export policy for Workflow/subagent sidecar artifacts: preserve and make usable, rebase known portable metadata, or intentionally drop/disable volatile artifacts.
3. After the fix, host-side resume of an exported session must not attempt to `cd`, read, or recover cache state from an inaccessible `/Users/agent/.claude/projects/...` path.
4. If preserving Workflow cache is the chosen policy, expensive completed Workflow agents from the contained run must be reusable after host resume without rerunning solely because the path moved.
5. If dropping volatile artifacts is the chosen policy, host Claude should degrade predictably with no misleading copied caches and docs should state the limitation.
6. Add focused tests around `exportAgentClaudeSessionBundle`/install behavior for Workflow sidecar paths or metadata, plus any permission-repair tests if that direction is chosen.
7. Update `docs/usage.md` so the `hazmat export claude session` contract covers dynamic sidecar/workflow artifacts and the chosen limitation or support guarantee.
notes:
2026-06-13 local live-wrapper hardening: check-claude-workflow-export-smoke now scans the exported host project sessions-index.json in addition to transcript and sidecar files for stale /Users/agent Claude project paths before host resume. scripts/test-entrypoint-guards.sh pins this evidence boundary. Live host-resume validation remains approval-gated.
2026-06-13 continuation audit: local code/docs/tests already encode the conservative Workflow export policy: portable JSON/JSONL metadata is rebased, opaque or malformed sidecar artifacts with agent paths are omitted, sessions-index is scanned, and docs/usage.md says cache reuse is best-effort. Remaining acceptance requires explicit approval for the live Claude Workflow export/resume smoke; do not claim host-resume validation from local tests alone.
2026-06-13 blocked classification: local implementation, docs, and hermetic tests cover the conservative Workflow export policy; remaining acceptance requires explicit approval and live execution of scripts/check-claude-workflow-export-smoke.sh --run --i-understand-this-runs-hazmat-claude-and-host-claude with usable Hazmat and host Claude CLIs. Do not close without the live host-resume evidence.

title: [epic] CLI-managed agent harness lifecycle
description:
Why:
Hazmat already installs and launches built-in agent code harnesses for the agent user, but lifecycle ownership is split across `hazmat bootstrap <harness>`, a coarse `hazmat status` summary, and per-harness implementation files. Users need a CLI UI that can answer "what is installed?", refresh harness code intentionally, and uninstall Hazmat-managed code artifacts without manually touching `/Users/agent`.

Scope:
- Add a first-class harness lifecycle CLI for built-in harnesses: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, and Hermes.
- Show per-harness status, including install/probe state, recorded Hazmat metadata, last curated import where applicable, credential/config hints, and next actions.
- Add explicit update commands that reuse the existing install-or-update paths and preserve current `hazmat bootstrap <harness>` compatibility.
- Add safe uninstall commands for Hazmat-owned harness code artifacts and host-owned metadata, preserving auth/profile/session data by default unless an explicit, modeled purge is added.
- Update `hazmat status`, docs, and manual testing so users discover the new lifecycle UI.

Non-goals:
- Adding new third-party harnesses.
- Supporting arbitrary plugin harness uninstall.
- Silently removing user-edited auth, profile, history, session, or provider data.
- Automating or controlling desktop apps.
design:
Recommended design:
1. Introduce a small harness lifecycle layer around `ManagedHarness`: status/probe, update, uninstall plan, and user-facing action hints. Keep harness-specific knowledge in the harness modules, not in the Cobra command.
2. Add a top-level CLI UI such as `hazmat harness status [id]`, `hazmat harness update <id|--all>`, and `hazmat harness uninstall <id>`. Keep `hazmat bootstrap <harness>` as a backwards-compatible alias/delegation path.
3. Render list status as a compact table and detail status as labeled fields. Include `--json` only if it fits existing CLI conventions during implementation.
4. Implement uninstall as plan/apply: enumerate declared Hazmat-owned code artifacts, show preserved user data, support `--dry-run`, and refuse ambiguous or drifted removals unless a force path is explicitly designed.
5. Update `tla/MC_HarnessLifecycle.tla` and `tla/08_harness_lifecycle.md` before code, because uninstall and richer harness recording change the verified lifecycle boundary.

Alternatives considered:
- Fold this into `hazmat bootstrap` and root `hazmat status`: lower implementation cost, but status/update/uninstall remain scattered and harder to discover.
- Full purge by default: simpler UX, but too risky because current imports and harness profiles may contain user-owned auth/session state.
acceptance_criteria:
- `hazmat harness status` shows every built-in harness with install/probe state, recorded state health, import/auth/config hints where relevant, and next action guidance.
- `hazmat harness status <id>` shows details including binary path or missing reason, version/probe result when available, state record/version, last import timestamp, and managed/preserved artifact boundaries.
- `hazmat harness update <id>` and `hazmat harness update --all` refresh supported harnesses through the existing installer paths and record harness state consistently; dry-run does not mutate agent home or host metadata.
- Existing `hazmat bootstrap` commands remain backward compatible and share the same lifecycle implementation.
- `hazmat harness uninstall <id>` removes only declared Hazmat-owned code artifacts and host-owned harness metadata by default, reports preserved user data, supports dry-run, and refuses ambiguous/drifted deletes without an explicit force path.
- Hermes manual-install behavior is represented honestly: status/update/uninstall do not pretend Hazmat can fetch or own upstream Hermes code unless that supply-chain design changes.
- The harness lifecycle TLA+ model and design note are updated first, and TLC reports "No error has been found" for the affected spec before implementation proceeds.
- Go tests cover CLI wiring, status rendering, lifecycle state changes, dry-run preservation, update delegation, uninstall safety/drift handling, and backwards compatibility for `hazmat bootstrap`.
notes:
Relevant current code:
- `hazmat/harness.go` defines `ManagedHarness`, state recording, and installed-harness formatting.
- `hazmat/bootstrap*.go` contains current install/update and per-harness setup behavior.
- `hazmat/bootstrap_install.go` already centralizes install-or-update execution.
- `hazmat/init.go` renders the current coarse root status.
- `hazmat/hook_cli.go` is a useful CLI precedent for status/install/uninstall UX.
- `hazmat/state.go` owns `~/.hazmat/state.json` and `HarnessState`.
- `tla/MC_HarnessLifecycle.tla` and `tla/08_harness_lifecycle.md` are the verified lifecycle boundary that must move before implementation.

description:

Open Design argv: qwen --yolo [--model ...], prompt on stdin, plain stdout stream.
Known risk areas: Qwen Code is Gemini-CLI-like but has its own auth/config paths, provider key names, model selection, daemon mode, extension compatibility, and approval semantics. Confirm state paths before any import or env delivery.

Required process:
- Start with the intake checklist bead and the existing-harness parity audit, then write the compatibility decision in this bead.

- If compatible, update required TLA+ specs before implementation and record TLC results.
- Implement full Hazmat support: built-in HarnessID, registry, bootstrap/install verification, run command, credential policy, asset policy, explain/session metadata, debug trace metadata, e2e fake-binary smoke, docs, and manual test notes.
- If not compatible, close this bead with the reason and create the enabling architecture bead it needs.
design: Compatibility decision: Qwen Code is compatible with Hazmat's foreground harness architecture. Initial support is the CLI surface only: qwen binary in agent ~/.local/bin, prompt/headless flags passed through, Hazmat may add --yolo when session.skip_permissions is enabled. Daemon/SDK/channel modes remain out of scope until service lifecycle work exists. Credential policy: no host ~/.qwen import in this patch; Qwen auth/config stays contained under /Users/agent/.qwen, with portable QWEN.md/extensions asset sync only.

title: Audit existing Hazmat harnesses against Open Design and market research
description:
Before adding new harnesses, compare Hazmat current support with Open Design definitions and the user-supplied market-priority research.
Additional research source: /Users/dr/.codex/attachments/f130aba7-cbea-4fec-8227-b40fd88054fa/pasted-text.txt.
This source is a popularity + integration-readiness ranking, not a literal Open Design runtime registry. It recommends near-term focus on Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, OpenCode, OpenHands, and Qwen Code, with Gemini as a possible swap-in depending on Google/free-tier demand.
Hazmat already supports Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, and Hermes. The main new priority from the research is Qwen Code plus a separate OpenHands/service-platform evaluation. Cline, Amp, Goose, Kilo Code, Aider, Continue, and Crush become strategic/opportunistic follow-up evaluations. OpenClaw remains monitor/service-platform scope.

Audit points:
- Compare Hazmat non-interactive argv shapes and prompt delivery assumptions for claude, codex, opencode, gemini, and hermes against current Open Design runtime defs.
- Check bootstrap versions, install source, and expected binary names or fallbacks.
- Check auth/profile paths and provider env-var overlap.
- Verify docs/harnesses.md examples still match current CLI behavior.
- Decide whether Hermes ACP mode is in scope for Hazmat or remains foreground-only.
- Confirm whether market top-three support is actually complete or needs parity follow-up beads.
- File discovered follow-ups instead of mixing parity fixes into new-harness work.
acceptance_criteria: A written parity note exists in the bead, and follow-up beads are linked for any drift found. The note explicitly says whether Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, and Hermes remain complete enough for the market-priority queue to move to Qwen/OpenHands.
notes: Parity audit 2026-06-01: Hazmat already has managed foreground support for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, and Hermes. Open Design/market research top-three overlap is complete enough to move to Qwen. Hermes remains intentionally foreground-only; ACP/gateway/service mode belongs to the separate service-lifecycle design queue, not a blocker for Qwen. No blocking parity drift found during this pass.
close_reason: Parity note recorded; existing supported harnesses are complete enough to proceed to Qwen.
