title: Define Hazmat harness intake checklist for Open Design candidates
description:
Create the reusable process that every Open Design harness candidate must pass before code lands.
Research source: /Users/dr/workspace/opendesign, branch codex/run-media-policy-doc, commit 9e794ec2, with local uncommitted work present. Treat it as read-only input until re-verified at implementation time.
Authoritative current registry files: apps/daemon/src/runtimes/registry.ts and apps/daemon/src/runtimes/defs/*.ts. README.md supported table is useful, but lags registry-only entries such as grok-build and trae-cli.

Checklist gate 1: source and invocation evidence.
- Re-read the Open Design runtime def and docs at implementation time.
- Record binary name, fallback binaries, version probe, non-interactive argv, prompt delivery path, stream/protocol format, model flags, cwd/workspace flag, and any extra allowed-dir behavior.
- Cross-check against upstream docs or local CLI help when available. Do not trust stale README rows over registry/source.

Checklist gate 2: Hazmat architecture fit.
- The candidate must be a user-facing coding harness, not only an API proxy, model provider, or helper library.
- Hazmat must be able to launch a meaningful foreground session. ACP/RPC-only runtimes require a Hazmat protocol-driver decision before per-harness support.
- Non-interactive smoke must be possible with real or fake binaries.
- Service, daemon, gateway, cron, dashboard, or browser-control modes are excluded until a service lifecycle model exists.

Checklist gate 3: install, auth, state, and rollback.
- Define bootstrap source, pin/checksum/signature strategy, or explicitly choose manual verification only.
- Identify host auth/profile files, agent-side materialization paths, provider env vars, Keychain/external references, and any account-specific sockets or daemons.
- Decide whether host import is supported. Default to no import when state includes MCP servers, hooks, skills with scripts, cron jobs, memories, or broad profile secrets.
- Document rollback behavior, including whether ordinary rollback preserves agent-home state and whether delete-user is the only supported reset.

Checklist gate 4: model-first governance.
- Adding a HarnessID or changing importability starts in tla/MC_HarnessLifecycle.tla and tla/08_harness_lifecycle.md.
- Adding or changing provider/file credential delivery starts in tla/MC_CredentialCapabilityLifecycle.tla and tla/13_credential_capability_lifecycle.md.
- Changing materialize/harvest/recovery starts in tla/MC_SecretStoreRecovery.tla and tla/12_secret_store_recovery.md.
- Changing setup/rollback persistent mutations starts in tla/MC_SetupRollback.tla and tla/01_setup_rollback_state_machine.md.
- Changing permission repair semantics starts in tla/MC_SessionPermissionRepairs.tla and tla/07_session_permission_repairs.md.
- Run TLC for affected specs and record No error has been found before implementation.

Checklist gate 5: implementation surface.
- Add HarnessID/spec/state version/managed registry entry.
- Add bootstrap command and install/detection path.
- Add run command, session flag plumbing, session metadata, explain JSON, shell completion, and docs links.
- Add credential registry rows or explicit no-import/no-provider decision.
- Add harness asset sync only for portable prompt assets; never blindly sync executable skills, hooks, MCP configs, memories, or token caches.
- Add debug trace spec and test coverage for the new managed harness.

Checklist gate 6: tests and docs.
- Unit tests for registry, bootstrap dry-run, command argv, env grants, explain metadata, docs examples, and credential inventory/migration where applicable.
- Extend scripts/e2e-harness-smoke.sh and TestHarnessSmokeCoversEveryManagedHarness with a fake binary that asserts cwd, argv, env, auth materialization, harvest, cleanup, and network-none composition as applicable.
- Update docs/harnesses.md, docs/manual-testing.md, docs/claude-tracing.md naming if generalized, docs/design-assumptions.md, README/usage surfaces, and release notes when landing.
acceptance_criteria:
The checklist above is treated as the dependency for every Open Design harness candidate bead.
Any later harness task that skips a gate must document the reason in that bead before implementation proceeds.
close_reason: Checklist and non-harness BYOK scope decision recorded in the queue beads.

title: [epic] Code harness integration queue from Open Design and market research
description:
Track Hazmat support for code harnesses using two inputs: Open Design runtime-registry evidence and the later popularity/integration-readiness research supplied by the user.

Open Design registry source: /Users/dr/workspace/opendesign, branch codex/run-media-policy-doc, commit 9e794ec2, with local uncommitted work present. Treat it as read-only input until re-verified at implementation time. Authoritative registry files are apps/daemon/src/runtimes/registry.ts and apps/daemon/src/runtimes/defs/*.ts; README.md can lag registry-only entries such as grok-build and trae-cli.
Additional research source: /Users/dr/.codex/attachments/f130aba7-cbea-4fec-8227-b40fd88054fa/pasted-text.txt.
This source is a popularity + integration-readiness ranking, not a literal Open Design runtime registry. It recommends near-term focus on Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, OpenCode, OpenHands, and Qwen Code, with Gemini as a possible swap-in depending on Google/free-tier demand.
Hazmat already supports Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, and Hermes. The main new priority from the research is Qwen Code plus a separate OpenHands/service-platform evaluation. Cline, Amp, Goose, Kilo Code, Aider, Continue, and Crush become strategic/opportunistic follow-up evaluations. OpenClaw remains monitor/service-platform scope.

Current overlap already managed by Hazmat: claude, codex, opencode, gemini, hermes.
Open Design registry adds candidate CLI/protocol adapters: cursor-agent, qwen, qoder, copilot, deepseek, grok-build, devin, kimi, kiro, kilo, vibe, trae-cli, pi.
Market research adds or emphasizes candidates not in the current Open Design registry: OpenHands, Cline, Amp, Goose, Aider, Continue, Crush, OpenClaw, plus Kilo Code as a market-relevant form of the existing OD kilo task.
Open Design BYOK/API proxy is not a code harness and should not become a HarnessID unless a separate provider-proxy feature is deliberately designed.

Queue policy:
1. Run the intake checklist before harness implementation work.
2. Do an existing-harness parity audit first because the market-recommended top three are already supported and may only need parity/docs/test follow-ups.
3. Treat Qwen Code as the first new foreground CLI candidate unless the parity audit finds a higher-risk existing-harness fix.
4. Treat OpenHands/OpenClaw-style server platforms as service-lifecycle architecture work before implementation, not as simple foreground harnesses.
5. For each harness, do compatibility assessment before implementation. If the architecture does not fit Hazmat, close the harness task with a written non-support decision and create the enabling architecture bead instead.
6. Full support means model-first changes where governed, bootstrap/install trust, credential policy, session command, metadata/explain output, e2e fake-binary or fake-service smoke, debug trace coverage, docs, manual test notes, and release-gate integration.
7. Do not add a user-provided plugin system. All supported harnesses remain maintainer-owned built-ins until the adapter RFC says otherwise.
acceptance_criteria:
Every Open Design registry harness and every market-research top/strategic candidate is either supported by Hazmat, queued with a compatibility/implementation bead, or explicitly closed as out of scope.
All compatible harnesses have model/proof, tests, e2e, docs, and release-gate tasks completed before this epic closes.
close_reason: All harness integration queue children are complete. Supported harnesses remained supported; Qwen/Cursor coverage was handled; service/protocol/market candidates were either implemented where appropriate or explicitly deferred with architecture notes, fake-test requirements, and deny-list hardening for host state roots.

title: Hermes memory/sessions/skills bleed across projects under one global HERMES_HOME
description:
hermesStateDir() is a single global '/Users/agent/.hazmat/hermes' with no project component (hazmat/bootstrap_hermes.go:19-21), HERMES_HOME is set unconditionally (applyHarnessStaticSessionEnv), and the native seatbelt grants read+write across the whole agent home every session regardless of -C.

Consequence: Hermes 'memories/', 'sessions/', and 'skills/' written while running 'hazmat hermes -C /projA' are fully readable and writable from a later 'hazmat hermes -C /projB' session. Hermes memory persists learned content (file contents, secrets seen, project structure), so this is a real cross-project confidentiality/correctness flow, not just shared scratch state.

This is undocumented in docs/plans/2026-05-30-hermes-harness-design.md (a Remaining Question was added pointing here). It is sharper for Hermes than for other harnesses because Hermes has a first-class persistent memory feature.

Fix: document explicitly that Hermes state is shared across all projects under the agent account and NOT isolated by -C; and/or give the managed root a per-project / per-workspace HERMES_HOME suffix (note: Hermes' HERMES_HOME also scopes its gateway PID file and systemd service name, per upstream docs, so per-project roots also reduce concurrent-session collisions). Decide whether v1's single-trust-domain assumption makes the shared root acceptable for the first release.
close_reason: Fixed in harness-lane-followups: Hermes now uses project-scoped managed HERMES_HOME paths, service-entrypoint rejection skips value-taking flag arguments before checking deferred commands, HarnessEnv comment covers non-secret state pointers, and Hermes is pinned in the non-native-TLS negative test. Verified go test ./... and MC_HarnessLifecycle TLC.

title: Hermes service-mode entrypoint rejection is an unsound argv heuristic
description:
rejectHermesDeferredEntrypoint/firstHermesEntrypoint (hazmat/hermes.go:77-99) decides gateway/dashboard/cron rejection from only the FIRST non-dash token forwarded after '--'.

False positive: 'hazmat hermes -- --profile gateway chat' returns entrypoint 'gateway' and is wrongly REJECTED, even though it is a valid chat session naming a profile/flag value 'gateway'. Any value-taking Hermes global flag whose value collides with a deferred keyword breaks a legitimate session.

False negative: 'hazmat hermes -- --profile X gateway' returns 'X' (first non-dash token) and is ALLOWED, so the real gateway subcommand slips through. Gateway/dashboard/cron enabled via the surviving HERMES_HOME/config.yaml, a HERMES_* env var, or initiated internally by a permitted subcommand are invisible to argv inspection entirely.

Impact: the base seatbelt policy allows 'network-inbound (local tcp "*:*")' (hazmat/session_policy_sbpl.go:201), so a slipped-through listener can actually bind locally. The doc presents this rejection as the deferral enforcement; today it is a leaky heuristic and a usability bug.

The existing test (hazmat/hermes_test.go:~168 '{"chat","gateway"}' and the --profile case) deliberately uses non-colliding values and never covers a colliding flag value.

Fix options: (a) parse with stop-at-flag-value semantics plus a positive subcommand allowlist; and/or (b) a pre-launch scan of the effective Hermes config for service-mode settings; or (c) explicitly document the rejection as argv-only best-effort (config/env-reachable service surfaces still run inside the seatbelt/native session and die with it, but are not 'rejected'). Add a test with a colliding flag value (e.g. '--profile gateway chat' must be ALLOWED; '--profile x gateway' must be REJECTED).
close_reason: Fixed in harness-lane-followups: Hermes now uses project-scoped managed HERMES_HOME paths, service-entrypoint rejection skips value-taking flag arguments before checking deferred commands, HarnessEnv comment covers non-secret state pointers, and Hermes is pinned in the non-native-TLS negative test. Verified go test ./... and MC_HarnessLifecycle TLC.

title: Evaluate trace package split after debug gating
description: Assess whether hazmat_debug trace implementation should move out of package main into an internal debugtrace package now that release builds omit trace. If accepted, split shared orchestration and platform backends without weakening strict configure/runtime preflight or changing the release binary surface.
notes: Evaluation for no-degradation architecture slice: keep this as a follow-up, not a merge blocker. The current hazmat_debug build tag already removes trace implementation from release/default builds. A package split would require broad callback/export seams because trace orchestration uses harness specs, parsers, session launch, explain rendering, shell quoting, and agent path constants from package main. That split is useful only if debug trace keeps growing; doing it now increases churn without improving the strict no-degradation guarantee.
close_reason: Completed: debug trace implementation moved into hazmat/internal/debugtrace behind hazmat_debug; hazmat/trace.go is now a thin main-package adapter for harness specs, main-only explain callbacks, host paths, and runSessionCommand. Release builds still omit trace; debug builds still require configure-debug-trace. Gates passed: go test ./..., go test -tags hazmat_debug ./... with temporary configured marker, Linux hazmat_debug compile with temporary marker, scripts/check-linux-compile.sh, scripts/check-cli-smoke.sh, scripts/check-fast.sh.

title: Evaluate per-session path-deny overlays for read-only project mounts
description: Redteam sandbox-mode review would prefer not to copy large repos before launching a reviewer harness. A possible hazmat-owned alternative is to mount the real project read-only while applying per-session deny overlays for repo-internal secret or sensitive paths (for example .envrc, group_vars/all.yml, auth profiles, password stores, large sensitive archives). This is only a proposal: hazmat development should make the final design decision because it changes path-policy semantics and likely requires TLA+ modeling/proof before implementation. External context: ops/redteam wants this as an alternative to full repo-copy for OPS-xd86.2 sandbox mode, alongside sandboxing-jmna network=none.
design:
Decision captured 2026-05-22: keep this bead open as a Hazmat evaluation/research item, but OPS/redteam architecture must not depend on live read-only mounts plus path-deny overlays.

Default workspace strategy: secret bytes absent, not secret bytes present but denied.

Practical ranking for OPS-style review packets:
1. Manifest-only materialization: use for packet/brokered review and high-sensitivity reviews. Only explicitly included files, diffs, and beads exist.
2. APFS clone plus delete/mask denied paths: likely best macOS sandbox workspace default if implemented carefully. It is cheap, point-in-time, preserves repo shape, avoids live host mutation exposure, and removes secret bytes before reviewer launch.
3. Filtered copy: portable fallback. Expensive, but conceptually simple.
4. Sparse worktree: useful only for tracked-file scopes. Insufficient for untracked secrets or repo-local state.
5. Live read-only mount plus path-deny overlay: evaluation only, not default. Path policy is weaker than content absence, especially with hardlinks, symlink/path normalization complexity, and live host-side mutation.

Redteam decision consequences:
- Prefer absent secret bytes over live path-deny because materialization avoids hardlink/path-alias, live-change, and proof-complexity hazards.
- Treat live path-deny overlays as experimental because they change Hazmat's project-view invariant and require TLA+ model/design work before any implementation.
- For redteam MVP: Rung 1 is manifest-only materialization; Rung 2 sandbox is APFS clone when available, filtered copy fallback, with denied paths removed or masked before Hazmat launch.
- Never use live path-deny overlays for sensitive reviews until Hazmat accepts and proves that mode.
- This bead is not a blocker for OPS-xd86.3; it remains an optimization/research path.
acceptance_criteria: Hazmat dev evaluates whether per-session deny overlays are safe and desirable compared with filtered copy, sparse worktree, APFS clone, or manifest-only materialization; if accepted, the design specifies deny-overrides-allow precedence for broad read-only mounts, interaction with -R/-C/session policy, glob/path normalization semantics, symlink and hardlink behavior, failure modes, machine-readable metadata, and teardown behavior; verified areas are updated through the relevant TLA+ model/design note before implementation; tests cover denied repo-internal secret paths under an otherwise read-only project mount, allowed non-secret reads, symlink traversal attempts, glob edge cases, and concurrent sessions.
close_reason: Decision recorded: reject live repo-internal path-deny overlays as default architecture; prefer manifest-only/APFS-clone/filtered-copy materialized project views where excluded sensitive bytes are absent before launch. See docs/plans/2026-06-12-path-deny-overlay-evaluation.md.

title: integration: php-composer
description:

title: integration: pnpm
description:
pnpm is 19.9% share of JS package managers (State of Frontend 2024) and 92-93% retention (SoJS 2024 — highest in the category). The content-addressable store at ~/.local/share/pnpm (Linux/macOS default) is the entire reason pnpm exists — every dependency install hardlinks from there into node_modules. Without read access, 'pnpm install' fails before resolving any deps.

Manifest-only. The node toolchain is already handled by the 'node' integration; pnpm just adds its store.

Key paths and env vars:
- read_dirs: ~/.local/share/pnpm (modern default), ~/Library/pnpm (macOS XDG variant when XDG_DATA_HOME is unset and ~/Library is preferred), ~/.pnpm-store (legacy)
- env_passthrough: PNPM_HOME (NOT YET in safeEnvKeys — add to integration_manifest.go:safeEnvKeys as a path-only key alongside CARGO_HOME and GEM_HOME)
- detect: pnpm-lock.yaml
- backup excludes: node_modules/, .next/, .turbo/, .nuxt/, out/, .vercel/, .pnpm-store/

This integration coexists with 'node' — both should activate together on a pnpm project. Check that mergeIntegrations dedups the node_modules / .next / .turbo excludes between them.
acceptance_criteria: 1) hazmat/integrations/pnpm.yaml exists, embeds, and passes 'hazmat integration validate'. 2) PNPM_HOME added to safeEnvKeys map in integration_manifest.go with comment. 3) Suggesting on a project with pnpm-lock.yaml produces both 'node' and 'pnpm'. 4) backup excludes from pnpm and node merge without duplicates (test in integration_manifest_test.go). 5) End-to-end: 'hazmat exec -- pnpm install' in a tiny fixture succeeds, no sandbox denials related to ~/.local/share/pnpm.
notes: Fixture: package.json with one dep ('lodash'), pnpm-lock.yaml. Verify hardlinks land in node_modules and the store path is in 'hazmat explain' Auto read-only.
close_reason: pnpm integration shipped in this commit. Verified pnpm install + node require() inside hazmat exec; node coexistence dedups shared excludes. PNPM_HOME added to safeEnvKeys as a path pointer.

title: integration: python-pip (plain pip + venv/virtualenv)
description:
pip is the majority Python tool (74% per JetBrains Python Survey 2024) — we ship python-uv (12%) and python-poetry (20%) but no plain-pip manifest. Users invoking 'pip install -r requirements.txt' from inside a hazmat session hit denials because ~/.cache/pip (wheel cache) and ~/.local/lib/python*/site-packages (user-site installs) are not in the agent's read scope.

Manifest-only — no resolver needed. The Python interpreter itself is found via the system / Homebrew python which is already covered by base policy.

Key paths and env vars:
- read_dirs: ~/.cache/pip, ~/.local/lib (covers user-site installs), ~/.pyenv if present (deferred — pyenv users often install python there)
- env_passthrough: VIRTUAL_ENV (already in safeEnvKeys)
- detect: requirements.txt OR requirements/*.txt OR setup.py OR pyproject.toml when neither uv.lock nor poetry.lock is present (avoid double-suggesting alongside python-uv / python-poetry — see integration_manifest.go suggestion ordering)
- backup excludes: .venv/, venv/, env/, __pycache__/, .pytest_cache/, .mypy_cache/, .ruff_cache/, *.pyc, dist/, *.egg-info/, build/

Mind the conflict with python-uv (uv.lock) and python-poetry (poetry.lock) — the manifest must only fire when neither lock file is present. Look at integration_manifest_test.go around line 686 and 718 for the existing suggestion tie-breaking pattern.
acceptance_criteria: 1) hazmat/integrations/python-pip.yaml exists, embeds in builtinIntegrationsFS, and passes 'hazmat integration validate' against the embedded copy. 2) Suggesting on a project with requirements.txt and no lock files produces python-pip (NOT python-uv or python-poetry). 3) Suggesting on a project with uv.lock OR poetry.lock does NOT produce python-pip. 4) Integration tests in integration_manifest_test.go cover the three-way suggestion arbitration (pip vs uv vs poetry). 5) End-to-end: 'hazmat exec -- pip install -r requirements.txt' against a tiny test fixture completes without sandbox denials (verify by 'log show --predicate sandbox' returning no new pip-process denies). 6) docs/integrations.md lists python-pip alongside python-uv / python-poetry.
notes: Test fixture: a /tmp project with requirements.txt of one wheel-only pure-Python pkg (e.g. 'requests==2.32.5'). Verify: pip install succeeds, .venv populated, no denials. Then add a poetry.lock and confirm python-pip is no longer suggested.
close_reason: python-pip integration shipped in commit 85c51ca. Three-way detection arbitration (pip vs uv vs poetry) verified with four new tests. Resolver shares resolvePythonIntegration with the other Python toolchains so /opt ancestor metadata is granted. Smoke test: offline pip install succeeds inside hazmat exec session. Online pip blocked only by an orthogonal TLS-cert-chain issue (Python ssl -> SecureTransport without MacOSNativeTLS grants), filed separately.

title: Built-in integration roadmap: top-10 stack gaps
description:
Add the 10 highest-leverage built-in integrations identified by the 2026-05-14 research pass against Stack Overflow 2025, JetBrains Dev Ecosystem 2024, GitHub Octoverse 2025, State of JS 2024, State of Frontend 2024, Modern C++ DevOps 2024, and the Anthropic / Pragmatic Engineer pieces on Claude Code's own stack.

Today hazmat ships 14: beads, elixir-mix, go, haskell-cabal, java-gradle, java-maven, node, opentofu-plan, python-poetry, python-uv, ruby-bundler, rust, terraform-plan, tla-java.

Gaps prioritized by (population size) × (agentic-dev relevance) × (sandbox-friction severity):

Batch 1 — manifest-only (read_dirs + excludes + env_passthrough, no resolver):
  1. python-pip — pip 74% of Python devs (JetBrains 2024); we have uv (12%) and Poetry (20%) but not the majority tool
  2. pnpm — 19.9% share (State of Frontend 2024), 92-93% retention (SoJS 2024 highest)
  3. php-composer — PHP 18.9% (SO 2025), Composer global at ~/.composer

Batch 2 — needs runtime resolver in integration_resolver.go (probe toolchain location, return AdditionalReadDirs):
  4. dotnet — C# 27.8% (#8 SO 2025), +22% YoY contributors (Octoverse 2025)
  5. swift / SwiftPM — 95% of iOS devs (SO 2024); macOS-native, highest platform affinity
  6. bun — ~16% of JS runtime users (SoJS 2024); Claude Code itself runs on Bun
  7. android-gradle — Kotlin 73% of Android devs (SO 2024); ANDROID_HOME + ~/.android distinct from java-gradle

Batch 3 — heavier design work (heterogeneous toolchains / cross-cutting):
  8. cmake / C++ — C++ 23.5% + C 22% (SO 2025); CMake 83% of C++ build share (Modern C++ DevOps 2024)
  9. flutter / dart pub — Dart 5.9% (SO 2025), 94.9% adoption in Flutter shops; pulls Flutter SDK + Android SDK + Xcode at once
  10. docker — 71.1% (SO 2025, +17pt YoY, largest jump in survey); UX surface on existing Tier 3 Docker Sandbox mode

Out of scope for this epic: conda (deferred #11 — re-evaluate after batch 1), sbt, Vite.

Per integration the deliverable is: (a) embedded YAML in hazmat/integrations/<name>.yaml passing 'hazmat integration validate', (b) where needed, a resolver entry in integration_resolver.go pinning AdditionalReadDirs from a runtime probe, (c) coverage in integration_resolver_test.go or integration_manifest_test.go, (d) at least one non-interactive smoke test ('hazmat exec' or 'hazmat codex exec') exercising the stack's primary install/build command without sandbox denials, (e) docs/integrations.md entry, (f) bumping the suggestion-detection allowlist in integration_manifest.go if needed.

No TLA+ spec update is expected for batch 1 and most of batch 2 — adding read_dirs and AdditionalReadDirs is pure data flowing through the existing MC_SeatbeltPolicy contract. CMake (toolchain branching) and docker (lives in MC_Tier3LaunchContainment scope) may need spec touches; flag those explicitly in their child tasks before implementing.

Done when: all 10 child issues closed, full integration test suite green, docs/integrations.md lists each new integration, and a sanity check (.hazmat/integrations.yaml in a stack-typical sample project) shows each one suggested and applies cleanly.
close_reason: All children completed

Profile-referencing keys are unaffected — they inherit from default_hosts as before, which is explicit config rather than a back-compat concession.

The fallback was only needed so pre-multi-key installs kept working. The user base is one person today, and force-migrating once produces a simpler codebase and a stronger TLA+ invariant.
design:
Design decisions (agreed 2026-04-22):

1. Remove 'hazmat config ssh set <path>' entirely. No deprecation alias. Users run 'hazmat config ssh add --name default --host <h> <path>' going forward.

2. loadConfig fails loud on the flat legacy shape. When 'ssh: {private_key, known_hosts}' appears without a Keys list, loadConfig returns an error containing the exact replacement YAML so the user can paste it and move on. No auto-rewrite — auto-converting an any-host fallback into 'ssh add --host ???' would either invent a host list or leave it empty (which is now illegal). Fail-once, paste-fix, move on.

3. Tracked separately from sandboxing-nm5o so review boundaries stay clean: sandboxing-nm5o is 'added profiles', this bead is 'retired the legacy fallback'. Separate commits, separate TLA+ diff, separate CHANGELOG entry.

Code drops:
- NormalizedKeys(): synthesis of a single-entry Keys list from flat PrivateKeyPath/Key/KnownHostsPath is removed. Returns Keys as-is or nil.
- ValidateProjectSSHConfig: inlineEmptyCount check becomes 'any inline key with empty hosts is rejected' regardless of key count.
- buildGitSSHWrapperScript: legacyAnyHostKey helper is removed; wrapper always emits a case-with-default-reject, never the bare any-host exec.
- selectSessionGitSSHKey: the len(cfg.Keys) == 1 && empty AllowedHosts fast-path is removed.
- runConfigSSHAdd: the 'cannot add a second key while X is configured as any-host legacy' migration-hint error becomes unreachable and is removed.
- runConfigSSHSet, runConfigSSHListKeys integration around 'ssh set', completeSSHSetKeyArgs, chooseSSHKeyCandidate, promptSSHKeyDirectory if only used by set: removed.

TLA+ changes (MC_GitSSHRouting):
- Remove LegacySingle, LegacyMultiInvalid predicates, and the LegacySingle branch from Normalize.
- Remove LegacyFallbackSingleOnly invariant.
- Add InlineKeysHaveDeclaredHosts: ready ⇒ every present inline key has a non-empty effective host set.
- Validate adds 'InlineKeyEmptyHosts' to its rejection set.
- State space shrinks slightly; coverage for legacy paths removed.

title: seatbelt: per-harness policies (least privilege per agent client)
description:
The current session_policy_sbpl.go emits one shared seatbelt policy for every harness (claude, codex, opencode, future gemini). This is the union of what any harness might need — which means each harness gets rules it doesn't actually use. Examples observed today (2026-04-22) while making codex work:

  - mach-lookup com.apple.SystemConfiguration.configd  (codex needs; claude doesn't — Node.js doesn't use SCDynamicStore)
  - file-read /Library/Keychains                       (codex needs for native TLS; claude uses OpenSSL, doesn't need)
  - ipc-posix-shm-read-data apple.shm.notification_center (codex Rust reqwest; claude doesn't)
  - system-socket AF_SYSTEM/SYSPROTO_CONTROL           (codex SCDynamicStore data path; claude doesn't)

Conversely, claude likely uses node-specific paths (Library/Caches/com.anthropic.claude-code, etc.) that codex doesn't touch.

Goal: emit a harness-scoped policy so each session only carries the minimum surface that its specific harness exercises. Compose from a small shared base + per-harness overlays.

Proposed shape:
  - keep session_policy_sbpl.go's compileDarwinSBPL signature, but pipe HarnessID (or a typed HarnessPolicy struct) into the function
  - extract the rules unique to codex (configd / Keychains / shm.notification_center / AF_SYSTEM) into a codexExtraSBPL section, gated on HarnessID == HarnessCodex
  - same shape for claude-only and opencode-only rules once we identify them
  - keep TLA+ MC_SeatbeltPolicy invariants intact: credential-deny set still last-match-wins regardless of which harness overlay is active
acceptance_criteria: A 'hazmat claude' session shows fewer seatbelt allows than 'hazmat codex' (verifiable by snapshotting the generated /tmp/hazmat-<pid>.sb file). Existing CredentialReadDenied / AgentContained invariants still pass under TLC for every harness variant. No harness regresses on functionality.
notes: Discovery driver: the codex unblocking work in commits dd89811..e9f2c0b added several broad rules to make codex's Rust+native-TLS chain work. Those rules don't belong in the policy applied to the Node-based claude harness.
close_reason: Landed in 3e94a75. Refactor: HarnessID added to sessionConfig; nativeSessionPolicy.MacOSNativeTLS gated by harnessUsesMacOSNativeTLS (codex only as of 2026-04-23). compileDarwinSBPL gates 10 codex-only allows behind that flag (configd, trustd.agent, SecurityServer, /System/Cryptexes, /Library/Keychains, /Library/Preferences/com.apple.security.plist, apple.shm.notification_center, AF_SYSTEM/SYSPROTO_CONTROL, login.keychain post-deny override). 4 new tests cover the gating + acceptance criterion (claude policy strictly smaller than codex by >=8 allows). MC_SeatbeltPolicy invariants unaffected (spec models 6 path sections only, not mach services).

title: Add reusable SSH profiles with cross-project sharing
description: Extend the multi-key SSH support (sandboxing-vmg1) with a top-level 'ssh_profiles' map in config.yaml so a named identity can be defined once and referenced from any project via 'profile: <name>'. Profiles carry the private key path, known_hosts, optional default_hosts, and optional description. Projects inherit default_hosts unless they override with --host. Inline keys (the current 'private_key:' form) remain supported; profiles are opt-in, not a replacement.
design:
Design decisions (agreed 2026-04-22):

1. Cascade-safe removal. 'hazmat config ssh profile remove <name>' refuses when one or more projects reference the profile; the error lists the referrers. '--force' detaches every project reference AND removes the profile in one operation. No silent dangling state.

2. Printed inheritance. 'hazmat config ssh add --profile <name>' without --host inherits profile.default_hosts and prints the inherited list in the confirmation output. Later widening of default_hosts is therefore visible in command history, not silent.

3. Inline keys stay. 'hazmat config ssh add <path>' without --profile continues to write inline 'private_key:' entries. Profiles are an additional mode, not a replacement.

4. One-agent-per-key even with shared profiles. Two project keys that reference the same profile still allocate separate per-session ssh-agent sockets. This keeps MC_GitSSHRouting's SocketsDistinctForPresent invariant unchanged and preserves the defense-in-depth rationale from the wrapper's socket binding.

5. Dangling profile references are rejected at config-load, not session-launch. ValidateProjectSSHConfig (or a new ValidateSSHProfiles walker) catches 'profile: ghost' entries when loadConfig parses the file.

6. Schema: 'profile' and 'private_key' on the same ProjectSSHKey is a validation error. Pick one.
acceptance_criteria: Top-level ssh_profiles: map with private_key, known_hosts, default_hosts, description. ProjectSSHKey.Profile field; when set, private_key and known_hosts must be empty. 'hazmat config ssh profile add | list | show | remove | rename' CLI. 'hazmat config ssh add --profile <name>' uses the profile identity and inherits default_hosts when --host is omitted; --host overrides. 'ssh profile remove' refuses while referrers exist and requires --force to cascade-detach. Dangling references rejected at config-load. MC_GitSSHRouting extended with ProfileNames constant, keyProfile variable, profileDefaultHosts variable, definedProfiles variable, and a NoDanglingProfileRefs invariant. Existing routing invariants (DeterministicRouting, OverlapRejectedAtConfigTime, LegacyFallbackSingleOnly, SocketsDistinctForPresent, NoCrossKey) continue to pass on effective (identity, hosts) pairs after profile resolution. tla/VERIFIED.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/usage.md, CHANGELOG.md updated.
notes:
Implementation landed across 4 commits on top of spec (0acab7b..5f51e30):

- 0acab7b tla: extend MC_GitSSHRouting with profile resolution layer (884,736 states)
- 2cade5e config: add ssh_profiles schema and profile-aware validation
- 718b7b1 session: resolve ssh profile references at session-time
- 64a3320 ux: add 'ssh profile' CLI and --profile flag on 'ssh add'
- 5f51e30 docs: document reusable SSH profiles in usage.md and CHANGELOG

All design decisions from the original bead honored:
(1) referrer-safe removal with --force cascade,
(2) printed inheritance in 'ssh add' confirmation,
(3) inline keys still supported,
(4) one agent per key even when two project keys share a profile,
(5) dangling refs rejected at config load,
(6) profile+inline on same key rejected at format validation.

Go tests passing end-to-end, full TLA+ suite passing. Bead should close
once manual testing completes.

title: Support multiple SSH keys per project with host-based routing
description: Add per-project support for multiple SSH keys, each with an explicit host allowlist. Primary use case: one key for github.com, a separate key for remote production hosts, stored in host-owned storage and never reachable from the agent HOME. Generalizes the current single-key project SSH model without regressing the single-key UX.
design:
Design decisions (agreed 2026-04-21):
1. Each key carries a mandatory 'hosts' list when a project has 2+ keys. Single-key configs retain today's 'any host' fallback.
2. One ssh-agent per key, one socket per key. The wrapper selects the socket by matching the destination host against each key's host-globs. Defense-in-depth: a wrapper-parsing bug can only mis-offer one key, not the whole set.
3. Config-set-time overlap detection — if two keys both match the same host/glob, refuse to save the config.
4. Retire 'hazmat config ssh set' in favor of 'ssh add --name <n> --host <h>'. Keep 'ssh set' for one release with a deprecation hint that rewrites it to 'ssh add --name default'.
5. TLA+-first: this is a new verified capability, so draft 'tla/MC_GitSSHRouting.tla' and the companion 'tla/10_git_ssh_routing.md' before writing Go. Run TLC before implementation.
6. Key routing invariants to prove:
   - DeterministicRouting: for any host, (config, host) maps to at most one key-or-reject outcome.
   - NoCrossKey: the selected key's IdentityAgent socket is only that key's socket (no shared socket).
   - OverlapRejectedAtConfigTime: a config with two host-matching keys is rejected before it can enter a session.
   - HostsOutsideAllowlistRejected: the wrapper rejects any host not matched by any key's host list.
7. Config schema becomes:
     projects:
       <projectDir>:
         ssh:
           keys:
             - name: github
               private_key: ...
               known_hosts: ...
               hosts: [github.com]
             - name: prod
               private_key: ...
               known_hosts: ...
               hosts: [prod.example.com, '*.prod.example.com']
   Migration: legacy single-key 'ssh: {private_key, known_hosts}' parses into a one-element list with 'hosts: []' (any-host semantics), preserving today's behavior.
8. Related but not blocking: sandboxing-n1xy (brokered transport) inherits this routing contract host-side when it lands. The routing spec should stay wrapper/broker-agnostic.
acceptance_criteria: Each project can carry N>=1 named SSH keys, each with a private_key + known_hosts + hosts list. Config-set rejects overlapping host specs across keys. Wrapper routes destination host to exactly one key's identity agent socket, or rejects. Single-key projects (including legacy configs) keep working without config migration. 'hazmat config ssh test --host <h>' reports which named key was used. TLA+ suite includes a new MC_GitSSHRouting module with DeterministicRouting, NoCrossKey, OverlapRejectedAtConfigTime, and HostsOutsideAllowlistRejected proved via TLC before Go changes land. tla/VERIFIED.md updated.
notes: Implementation landed across 5 commits (2479f2c..7edbcba): spec stub, schema, runtime+wrapper, CLI, spec wiring. TLC clean on 193,536 states; full Go test suite passing; full TLA+ suite passing end to end. Brokered transport work (sandboxing-n1xy) inherits this routing contract when it arrives.

title: Resolve security-sensitive host tools without ambient PATH
description: Closes GitHub issue #7 (https://github.com/dredozubov/hazmat/issues/7). Homebrew coreutils on PATH shadows /bin/chmod; GNU chmod doesn't understand macOS's +a/-a ACL syntax, so ACL repair fails with 'exit status 1'. More broadly, hazmat currently resolves chmod, chown, ls, sudo, and git via ambient PATH, making the user's shell setup a trust input for a security tool. Fix with a centralized hostexec wrapper using absolute paths for system utilities and a fixed-allowlist git resolver. No process-global PATH mutation — intentional PATH-dependent behavior (vim, docker, brew, agent-side PATH) stays intact.
acceptance_criteria:
- hostexec package exposes absolute-path wrappers for: /usr/bin/sudo, /bin/chmod, /bin/ls, /usr/bin/dscl, /sbin/pfctl, /bin/launchctl, /usr/bin/uname, /usr/bin/script, /usr/bin/diff
- git resolved via fixed allowlist (/opt/homebrew/bin/git → /usr/local/bin/git → /usr/bin/git), frozen once per process; no /usr/bin/git hardcode
- newSudoCommand (exec.go:25) invokes /usr/bin/sudo absolutely
- integration_resolver.go:1139,1142 (Homebrew Cellar chmod) routes through hostexec
- ensureACL / removeACL / readACLs (from refactor) use hostexec for chmod and ls
- CI guard forbids bare exec.Command("chmod"/"chown"/"ls"/"sudo"/...) outside hostexec; decision on grep vs go/analysis pass documented in PR
- docs/design-assumptions.md gains a 'Tool resolution' section that explicitly separates hazmat's host-side exec PATH from the agent-PATH init writes into .zshrc; prior /usr/bin/git-as-shim claim removed
- manual verification: PATH=/opt/homebrew/opt/coreutils/libexec/gnubin:$PATH hazmat claude completes ACL repair successfully
- tla/check_suite.sh passes (change is below the concrete-IO boundary per tla/VERIFIED.md:34)
notes: The no-blanket-PATH decision comes from verification of four intentionally PATH-dependent call sites: config.go:583 ($EDITOR), sandbox.go:421 (docker lookup), stackcheck.go:424 (brew fallback), config_agent.go:111 (host git identity). Process-global os.Setenv would silently break all four. Also: on this dev machine /usr/bin/git is Apple Git 2.50.1 while the user's `git` is Homebrew 2.53.0 — the Xcode shim does NOT route to Homebrew, so naive /usr/bin/git substitution would downgrade git features. Allowlist resolver preserves the user's actual git.
close_reason: PATH hardening landed in 689ef98, closing GitHub #7. hostexec.go introduces absolute-path constants for all macOS base-system utilities plus a cached fixed-allowlist git resolver. /usr/bin/sudo is the first binary absolutely resolved; once entered, sudoers secure_path handles the rest. No process-global PATH mutation — verified the four intentionally PATH-dependent call sites ($EDITOR, docker, brew, host git identity via the allowlisted git) stay working. scripts/check-hostexec.sh wired into CI, forbids bare exec.Command on 13 system utilities outside hostexec.go. design-assumptions.md 'Tool resolution' section documents the trust separation between host-side hazmat exec and agent-side PATH. tla/check_suite.sh passes (9/9). All tests pass including the updated exec_test.go / git_safe_directory_test.go cases that previously baked in 'sudo' as a literal.

title: Refactor ACL grant/row modeling and centralize ensure/remove ACL invocation
description: ACL entries are built ad hoc in devGroupACLEntry (workspace_acl.go:17) and homeTraverseACLEntry (init.go:1406) using the chmod-input dialect, while aclOutputHasDevACL matches a different ls-output dialect with a permissive substring parser. Check-then-apply is copy-pasted across seven call sites; chmod -a is duplicated three times. Split input/output types, make the dialect normalization explicit, consolidate call sites. Pure refactor — no behavior delta beyond the Phase 0 semantic fix. Surfaced while analyzing GitHub issue #7 (https://github.com/dredozubov/hazmat/issues/7).
acceptance_criteria:
- ACLGrant type for chmod-input specs (principal, kind, perms, inherit); three canonical instances replace the three existing entry producers
- ACLRow type for parsed ls-output entries; one tolerant parser replaces aclOutputHasDevACL and the homeHasAgentTraverseACL grep
- Row.Satisfies(Grant) predicate carries the execute↔search / read↔list / write↔add_file+add_subdirectory+... normalization table in one reviewable place
- ensureACL / removeACL helpers take an explicit aclInvoker interface; direct-exec (file-owner) and sudo-routed (elevated) invokers are distinct implementations — no sentinel nil
- seven call sites migrated: workspace_acl.go:223,292,305,329, init.go:1415, rollback.go:347, migrate.go:75,119
- no behavior change beyond what Phase 0 landed
- tla/check_suite.sh passes
close_reason: Refactor landed in 802ba63 on top of semantic fix b9dd06a. New acl.go introduces ACLGrant (chmod-input dialect, three canonical vars), ACLRow (ls-output dialect, proper tokenizing parser with 'inherited' flag handling), Row.Satisfies + Row.GrantsPerm bridging the two dialects via aclPermAliases (the single reviewable normalization table). aclInvoker interface with directACLInvoker / sudoACLInvoker — no sentinel nil. Eight call sites migrated (user listed 7): workspace_acl.go (4), init.go (2, including setupHomeDirTraverse that wasn't in the original count), rollback.go (1), migrate.go (2); git_preflight.go repair-command string now uses grant.String(). Tests rewritten: 31 cases covering row parsing, Satisfies, GrantsPerm, alias table, multi-line scoping, inherited flag, grant string format. tla/check_suite.sh passes (9/9).

title: Fix ACL detection to inspect directory ACLs correctly and accept search-normalized traverse output
description: pathHasDevACL in workspace_acl.go:45 uses `ls -le` without `-d`, so for directories it inspects children instead of the directory's own ACL. homeHasAgentTraverseACL in init.go:1423 greps for `allow execute` but macOS normalizes execute→search on directory ACLs. Both are silent correctness bugs masked by mode-bit fallbacks; must land before the centralization refactor so each is bisectable. Surfaced while analyzing GitHub issue #7 (https://github.com/dredozubov/hazmat/issues/7).
acceptance_criteria:
- pathHasDevACL uses ls -leOd when path is a directory
- homeHasAgentTraverseACL accepts both 'allow execute' and 'allow search' tokens on directories
- parser tests cover: user: vs group:, allow vs deny, inherited vs non-inherited, directory-normalized (search/list/add_file) vs file-rendered (execute/read), and empty-ACL (no 0: line) cases
- PR documents audit of five dependent call sites: init.go:756, rollback.go:342, migrate.go:112, git_preflight.go:53, test.go:532 — which were previously masking or fighting the bug
- tla/check_suite.sh passes
close_reason: Semantic ACL detection fix landed in b9dd06a. Audit of five dependent call sites: init.go:756 was cosmetic (wrong-but-equivalent UI message when ACL was present). rollback.go:342 and migrate.go:112 were latent bugs — both silently skipped removing the traverse ACL during rollback/down-migration because the presence check always returned false post-application; now cleaned up correctly. git_preflight.go:53 and test.go:532 now report correctly on empty or recently-cleared directories instead of false negatives. Tests: 17 new parser cases covering principal scoping, allow/deny, inherit flags, directory vs file rendering, empty output, multi-line masking. tla/check_suite.sh passes (9/9 specs, all No error has been found).

title: Detection/messaging: distinguish shared-daemon-likely vs private-daemon-likely
description: When Docker artifacts are detected, improve routing messages by distinguishing projects that likely depend on the shared host daemon from self-contained projects that work with a private daemon. Currently all Docker artifacts are treated identically (session.go:872-879). Shared-daemon projects should get an explicit message explaining why Tier 3 is wrong for them and offering code-only mode. Private-daemon projects continue routing to Tier 3 normally. Ambiguous projects fall back to explicit user choice.
design: Heuristic signals for shared-daemon-likely: (1) external networks in compose files (networks.X.external: true), (2) Traefik Docker-provider labels, (3) scripts that docker compose up another project (like dev-up.sh booting docker-infra), (4) references to containers from other projects (e.g. shared-postgres). Private-daemon-likely: self-contained Compose with no external networks, or devcontainer with Docker fields. Ambiguous: mixed signals, fall back to user prompt or suggest hazmat config docker. Heuristics inform messaging only — they do not auto-decide. The routing decision still comes from --docker flag or persistent config.
close_reason: Added shared-daemon heuristics and explicit Docker routing errors

title: CLI/config: add persistent docker=none per-project setting

Replace with: (1) --docker=none flag for one-off code-only sessions, (2) hazmat config docker none -C /path/to/project for persistent per-project declaration stored in ~/.hazmat/config.yaml, (3) --docker=auto (default) preserves current detection behavior, (4) --docker=sandbox forces Tier 3. The config.go schema needs extension — current config set surface is whitelist-based (config.go:398) and does not support this. A dedicated hazmat config docker subcommand reads cleaner than generic config set.
design: Flag space: --docker=auto|none|sandbox. auto = current behavior (detect and route). none = code-only session, no Docker access, persists if set via config subcommand. sandbox = force Tier 3. Storage: ~/.hazmat/config.yaml under a projects map keyed by canonical path. CLI: hazmat config docker [auto|none|sandbox] -C <project-dir>. title: TLA: MC_CredentialCapabilityLifecycle omits OpenCode (cross-spec harness-set asymmetry)
description:

title: Hermes: GH_TOKEN delivered to autonomous harness with no scoping or self-push guidance
description:
applyGitHubSessionCapability (hazmat/github_capability.go:~76-105, injection ~97) is harness-agnostic: '--github' injects the full stored GH_TOKEN into cfg.HarnessEnv for any harness, and '--github' is exposed for Hermes identically to Claude.

For an autonomous harness, GH_TOKEN + project write = an agent that can push/open PRs without a human in the loop, and (per sandboxing-* / the whole-process env note) the token is inherited by every Hermes skill/MCP/hook subprocess. Token scope is set at mint time by the user, so this is a guidance/hardening gap, not a code defect.

Fix: add a session-contract/credential note that GH_TOKEN in a Hermes session is consumed by autonomous in-process code; recommend a fine-grained/read-only token for Hermes; consider a louder confirmation when '--github' is combined with the Hermes harness. Document the self-push risk.

title: Hermes: no per-harness uninstall/reset and no managed-root version migration
description:
Two related gaps in the Hermes managed state root lifecycle.

1) No Hermes-specific removal. The only removal path is full 'hazmat rollback'; rollback-keep-user preserves /Users/agent/.hazmat/hermes (RollbackWithoutDeleteUserPreservesArtifacts), so a user cannot cleanly remove just the accumulated Hermes state (which can hold agent-created creds in .env and cross-project memory/sessions — see sandboxing-mzfk). Only '--delete-user' clears it, which is far broader than 'reset Hermes'.

2) No managed-root schema versioning. hermesHarnessStateVersion='1' (harness.go Spec/RecordInstalled) is a write-only presence marker — nothing reads it back to gate behavior (contrast harnessAssetsStateVersion, which is read), and core pendingMigrations only operates on knownVersions. So if a future Hermes changes its on-disk HERMES_HOME layout there is no migration or incompatibility-detection path.

Fix: add a Hermes state-removal story (e.g. 'hazmat bootstrap hermes --remove' or a documented manual cleanup) and a design note that HERMES_HOME has no schema versioning; decide whether v1 should detect/refuse an incompatible managed root or document it as best-effort needing manual reset across Hermes upgrades.
close_reason: Added Hermes-specific reset, documented the reset/layout-version boundary, and applied status diagnostics that read harness state versions. Verified with go test ./... and MC_HarnessLifecycle TLC.
