title: flutter integration scope: name + Dart-only coverage
description:
Decision: name the integration 'flutter' rather than 'dart-pub', and have it cover plain Dart projects too. Trade-offs evaluated:

(+) 'flutter' is the higher-recognition name; Flutter projects dominate Dart usage (Dart 94.9% inside Flutter shops per Flutter CTO Report 2024).
(+) Plain Dart projects use the same ~/.pub-cache and pubspec.yaml as Flutter projects — the read_dir + detect set is identical.
(-) Slight semantic mismatch: a pure-Dart server project gets a 'flutter' integration. Naming-driven confusion, not functional.

Rejected alternative: rename to 'dart-pub' and require a separate 'flutter' integration that probes the Flutter SDK additionally. Would split a 2-line manifest into two with overlapping detection — more code than the naming-clarity buys.

Outcome: pubspec.yaml triggers 'flutter'. Resolver probes flutter SDK if available; falls back to manifest dirs (~/.pub-cache) when not.
close_reason: Current integration already implements the recorded decision: hazmat/integrations/flutter.yaml is named flutter, detects pubspec.yaml, grants pub/Dart cache paths, and integration_resolver.go documents/proves fallback behavior for pure-Dart projects when flutter is not on PATH. docs/STACKS.md and docs/integrations.md reflect the scope.

title: integration: flutter / dart pub
description:
Dart at 5.9% (SO 2025), Dart 94.9% adoption inside Flutter shops (Flutter CTO Report 2024 / Walturn). Flutter is heavyweight — it bundles Dart, ships its own Android SDK manager hook, and on macOS depends on Xcode for iOS builds.

The Flutter SDK is typically installed at ~/development/flutter or ~/fvm/versions/* (FVM-managed) or via Homebrew flutter (rare). 'flutter pub get' writes to ~/.pub-cache. 'flutter build apk' triggers gradle assembleRelease (overlap with android-gradle integration). 'flutter build ios' triggers Xcode (overlap with swift integration).

Needs a resolver that locates the Flutter SDK and exposes its bin dir and bundled dart-sdk. Coexistence: when a flutter project is detected, the android-gradle integration should also activate for the android/ subdir, and swift for ios/ — verify the merge dedups overlapping ANDROID_HOME / DEVELOPER_DIR grants.

Key paths and env vars:
- read_dirs (manifest): ~/.pub-cache, ~/.dart, ~/.dart-tool
- read_dirs (resolver): Flutter SDK root (~/development/flutter or 'which flutter' walking up to the SDK root), the bundled bin/cache/dart-sdk
- env_passthrough: FLUTTER_ROOT (add to safeEnvKeys), PUB_CACHE (add to safeEnvKeys)
- detect: pubspec.yaml (also matches plain Dart projects — that is fine; flutter-only projects can be distinguished if needed via 'flutter:' SDK constraint, but plain dart projects benefit from the same pub-cache grant so the integration name 'flutter' may be misleading — consider 'dart-pub' if scope is widened. Decision needed: keep 'flutter' scoped, or rename to 'dart-pub' and let it work for both)
- backup excludes: build/, .dart_tool/, .flutter-plugins, .flutter-plugins-dependencies, ios/Pods/, android/.gradle/, android/build/
acceptance_criteria: 1) Design decision recorded (bd decision) on scope: 'flutter' vs 'dart-pub'. Default recommendation: name it 'flutter' but cover plain Dart projects too (the read_dir set is the same). 2) hazmat/integrations/flutter.yaml exists, validates. 3) Resolver locates Flutter SDK and exposes bin/cache/dart-sdk. 4) FLUTTER_ROOT and PUB_CACHE added to safeEnvKeys. 5) Test in integration_resolver_test.go for SDK probe success and missing-SDK fallback. 6) End-to-end: 'hazmat exec -- flutter pub get' on a 'flutter create' fixture succeeds. 7) Manual smoke (documented in docs/integrations.md, not automated): full 'flutter build apk' requires android-gradle to also activate — confirm both fire.
notes: Verify FVM (Flutter Version Management) interaction by checking that the resolver handles ~/fvm/versions/<ver>/ as a flutter root. Defer FVM-specific support if it complicates the design.
close_reason: flutter integration shipped. Resolver covers SDK probe and missing-SDK fallback (two unit tests). Partial end-to-end: dart pub get inside hazmat exec reaches package resolution with ~/.pub-cache + Flutter SDK visible in Auto read-only. Network TLS fails (orthogonal MacOSNativeTLS gap); flutter SDK's git ownership check fails for sandboxed agent (documented as warning, with workaround). Manifest warnings document both known limitations.

title: integration: docker — finalize UX on top of existing Tier 3 Docker Sandbox mode
description:
Docker at 71.1% in SO 2025 (#1 tool, +17pt YoY — largest single-year jump of any tech). Hazmat already has Docker Sandbox mode (Tier 3, governed by MC_Tier3LaunchContainment) — this is NOT a YAML-only manifest. The work here is the UX layer that bridges 'I have a Dockerfile / docker-compose.yml in my project' to 'hazmat suggests --docker=sandbox automatically'.

Status check: the niche-sieve session output during the python-uv work already showed 'Docker files detected: docker-compose.yml. Docker commands will not work in native containment. - If this session needs Docker, use: hazmat exec --docker=sandbox -C ... -- <command>'. So detection is wired up. Gaps to close:

1. A 'docker' built-in integration manifest that ONLY adds env passthrough for DOCKER_HOST and DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY (path pointers — add to safeEnvKeys) and backup excludes (.docker/, etc.). It does NOT widen read_dirs in native mode (Docker only works in Tier 3 sandbox mode anyway).
2. Detection should differentiate Dockerfile-only projects (could potentially be built in Tier 3) from docker-compose projects (need the daemon socket, only Tier 3 works).
3. The 'hazmat exec --docker=sandbox' suggestion should be promoted from 'note' to 'suggested integration' in the session resolve summary so users see it in the same place as other integrations.

TLA+ scope: any change to Tier 3 launch planning / gating belongs in MC_Tier3LaunchContainment.tla per CLAUDE.md. This task likely does NOT change Tier 3 launch behavior, only the manifest/UX above it — confirm before merging.

Decision needed: should 'docker' integration auto-trigger Tier 3 mode when a Dockerfile/compose file is detected, or remain explicit (--docker=sandbox)? Recommend keeping it explicit (auto-mode-switch surprises users with different containment semantics).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Design decision recorded (bd decision): does docker integration auto-trigger Tier 3 mode or stay explicit? 2) hazmat/integrations/docker.yaml exists, scoped narrowly: env_passthrough DOCKER_HOST + DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY, backup excludes only (.docker/, *.dockerfile.swp). 3) DOCKER_HOST + DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY added to safeEnvKeys with path-pointer comments. 4) Detection on Dockerfile OR docker-compose.yml OR docker-compose.yaml OR compose.yml. 5) Session-resolve summary promotes the existing 'use --docker=sandbox' note into the standard integration listing. 6) MC_Tier3LaunchContainment.tla unchanged (no Tier 3 launch behavior change). 7) End-to-end DEFERRED to manual: a docker-compose-based project shows the docker integration in 'hazmat explain' alongside the existing Docker Sandbox note.
notes: Cross-reference with the niche-sieve session output already showing 'Docker files detected: docker-compose.yml. Docker commands will not work in native containment.' — that lives in session resolve output. Find where that is emitted (grep 'Docker files detected') and route the same data through the integration suggestion path.
close_reason: docker integration shipped as a narrow YAML surface on top of the existing Tier 3 Docker Sandbox mode. env_passthrough DOCKER_HOST + DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY (inert in native mode), backup excludes, warning pointing at --docker=sandbox. No read_dirs because the Docker daemon is intentionally unavailable in native containment. MC_Tier3LaunchContainment unchanged. Two new detection tests cover Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml. Deferred: unifying the session.go:1810 'Docker files detected' note with the integration listing — UX polish, not a containment concern.

title: integration: cmake / C and C++
description:
C++ at 23.5% + C at 22% (SO 2025) — combined this is one of the largest unaddressed cohorts. CMake at 83% market share among C++ build tools (Modern C++ DevOps 2024). No current hazmat coverage.

Heavier design work: C/C++ toolchains are heterogeneous (Xcode CommandLineTools clang at /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/clang, Homebrew llvm at /opt/homebrew/Cellar/llvm, Homebrew gcc, conan/vcpkg-managed). The resolver must pick an active compiler and surface the right toolchain prefix. Out of scope for this task: conan, vcpkg, meson — those each warrant their own integration if data justifies (current SO data does not).

Key paths and env vars:
- read_dirs (manifest): ~/.cmake/packages (package registry), /opt/homebrew/Cellar/cmake (Homebrew cmake — already in base via /opt/homebrew but explicit grant aids ancestor metadata), /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools (already in base)
- read_dirs (resolver): output of 'xcode-select -p' for active SDK; output of 'brew --prefix llvm' if Homebrew llvm in use; CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH directories
- env_passthrough: CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH, CC, CXX (NOTE: CC/CXX may contain absolute paths to compiler — safe as path pointers; add with comment), CMAKE_GENERATOR
- detect: CMakeLists.txt
- backup excludes: build/, cmake-build-*/, CMakeFiles/, CMakeCache.txt, _deps/, install/

TLA+ touch-point check: does adding a C/C++-class compiler invocation (which forks many subprocesses, writes to /tmp, links shared libs) need MC_SeatbeltPolicy update? The base policy already allows process-exec on the project dir, /usr/bin, /opt/homebrew, /Library/Developer — typical compile/link should fit. If link step needs to read /System frameworks beyond what MacOSNativeTLS already grants, surface that. Flag this in the implementation PR.
acceptance_criteria: 1) hazmat/integrations/cmake.yaml exists, validates. 2) Resolver in integration_resolver.go locates the active toolchain (Xcode CLT or Homebrew llvm) and returns prefix in AdditionalReadDirs. 3) CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH / CC / CXX / CMAKE_GENERATOR added to safeEnvKeys with explicit 'path pointer or build-mode flag' justification comments. 4) Test in integration_resolver_test.go with both Xcode-CLT and Homebrew-llvm fakes. 5) End-to-end: 'hazmat exec -- cmake -B build && cmake --build build' against a hello-world CMakeLists.txt + main.cpp fixture succeeds. 6) Check the MC_SeatbeltPolicy spec is unaffected; if any new file-read* domain appears in the SBPL output that the spec doesn't model, update the spec and re-run check_suite.sh before merging.
notes: Smoke fixture: project_root with CMakeLists.txt (project(hi CXX); add_executable(hi main.cpp)) + main.cpp (int main() { return 0; }). Run cmake -B build then cmake --build build. Verify no denials, confirm /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/clang resolves via ancestor metadata.
close_reason: cmake integration shipped. Resolver dual-probes cmake + xcode-select. End-to-end: cmake configure + build on hello-world fixture succeeds inside hazmat exec. CC/CXX correctly stay out of safeEnvKeys per TestSafeEnvKeysExcludesDangerousKeys (flag-injection-equivalent); inline comment documents the cmake -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER= alternative.

title: integration: swift / SwiftPM (macOS-native)
description:
Swift at 5.4% in SO 2025 but 95% of iOS devs (SO 2024). Hazmat is macOS-native, so this stack has the highest platform affinity. SwiftPM caches built artifacts under ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData (when built via Xcode) and stores its own caches under ~/Library/Caches/org.swift.swiftpm and ~/Library/org.swift.swiftpm.

Needs a resolver to locate the active Xcode/CLT toolchain (xcode-select -p output), since users may have Xcode installed at /Applications/Xcode.app or use only the Command Line Tools (already in base policy).

Resolver returns the toolchain root (which contains usr/bin/swift, usr/lib/swift) plus the Library/Developer subtree.

Key paths and env vars:
- read_dirs (manifest): ~/Library/Caches/org.swift.swiftpm, ~/Library/org.swift.swiftpm, ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData
- read_dirs (resolver): output of 'xcode-select -p' (e.g. /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer or /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools — the latter is in base policy already, so dedup)
- env_passthrough: DEVELOPER_DIR (add to safeEnvKeys — path pointer to Xcode root)
- detect: Package.swift OR *.xcodeproj OR *.xcworkspace (xcodeproj/xcworkspace are dirs not files — check if hazmat detect handles dirs; if not, look for project.pbxproj inside them)
- backup excludes: .build/, .swiftpm/, DerivedData/, *.xcodeproj/xcuserdata/, *.xcworkspace/xcuserdata/

This integration is darwin-only — use the session.platforms.darwin block in the manifest.
acceptance_criteria: 1) hazmat/integrations/swift.yaml exists, validates, and is darwin-only (session.platforms.darwin scoped). 2) integration_resolver.go has 'swift' entry with Resolve that calls 'xcode-select -p', returns Developer dir in AdditionalReadDirs and DEVELOPER_DIR in ResolvedEnv. 3) Resolver fallback path when xcode-select fails: just use the manifest dirs. 4) Test in integration_resolver_test.go with fakeIntegrationProbe. 5) Detection fires on Package.swift. 6) End-to-end: 'hazmat exec -- swift build' on a 'swift package init --type executable' fixture succeeds. 7) DEVELOPER_DIR added to safeEnvKeys.
notes: Smoke project: 'swift package init --type executable' produces Package.swift + Sources/. Build expected to read DerivedData and the resolver-detected toolchain. If 'xcode-select -p' returns /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools (already base), the resolver should still emit it as AdditionalReadDirs and let the merge dedup.
close_reason: swift integration shipped. xcode-select resolver probe with fallback covered by two unit tests. End-to-end: 'swift build --disable-sandbox' inside hazmat exec on a swift package init fixture produces a runnable binary. Manifest carries a warning about SwiftPM's nested-sandbox EPERM and the --disable-sandbox / SWIFTPM_DISABLE_SANDBOX workaround.

title: integration: dotnet (.NET SDK + NuGet)
description:
C# at 27.8% (SO 2025 #8) and +22% YoY contributors (Octoverse 2025) — no current hazmat coverage. The dotnet CLI writes globally to ~/.nuget/packages (package cache), ~/.dotnet (SDK install + telemetry + tool cache when installed via script), and uses ~/.local/share/NuGet for older configs.

Needs a resolver (integration_resolver.go) because the SDK location varies: Homebrew (/opt/homebrew/Cellar/dotnet*), Apple Silicon official installer (/usr/local/share/dotnet), or per-user (~/.dotnet). The resolver should probe 'dotnet --info' or fallback to DOTNET_ROOT / standard install paths.

Resolver returns AdditionalReadDirs = [<sdk root>] and ResolvedEnv with DOTNET_ROOT pointing at the resolved SDK so the agent's dotnet invocation finds it.

Key paths and env vars:
- read_dirs (manifest): ~/.nuget, ~/.dotnet, ~/.local/share/NuGet
- read_dirs (resolver): SDK root from probe
- env_passthrough: DOTNET_ROOT (add to safeEnvKeys), NUGET_PACKAGES (add to safeEnvKeys)
- detect: *.csproj OR *.fsproj OR *.vbproj OR global.json OR Directory.Build.props (check if integration_manifest.go detect supports globs — if not, list specific common files; see existing detect patterns)
- backup excludes: bin/, obj/, .vs/, *.user, TestResults/, packages/
acceptance_criteria: 1) hazmat/integrations/dotnet.yaml exists and validates. 2) integration_resolver.go has 'dotnet' entry with Resolve callback that probes dotnet --info or DOTNET_ROOT, returns SDK prefix in AdditionalReadDirs and DOTNET_ROOT in ResolvedEnv. 3) Test in integration_resolver_test.go using fakeIntegrationProbe pattern covering both probe-success and Homebrew-fallback paths. 4) Suggestion fires on project containing global.json or *.csproj. 5) End-to-end: 'hazmat exec -- dotnet new console -o /tmp/hello && dotnet build /tmp/hello' completes without denials. 6) DOTNET_ROOT and NUGET_PACKAGES added to safeEnvKeys.
notes: Fixture: 'dotnet new console' output. Homebrew dotnet on M-series may be at /opt/homebrew/opt/dotnet/libexec or /usr/local/share/dotnet — confirm by checking 'brew --prefix dotnet' on a test machine.
close_reason: dotnet integration shipped; also fixes the /opt ancestor metadata gap in base policy that bit every Homebrew-symlinked tool. Verified end-to-end: dotnet new + build + run inside hazmat exec prints Hello, World!.

title: integration: android-gradle
description:
Kotlin at 73% of Android devs (SO 2024). hazmat has java-gradle but Android-specific paths ($ANDROID_HOME defaulting to ~/Library/Android/sdk on macOS, ~/.android emulator/keystore, ~/.gradle/caches/transforms with Android plugin artifacts, NDK toolchains) are out of scope for the JVM-generic integration. Building an Android project from inside hazmat today fails on first 'gradle assembleDebug' because the Android SDK platforms/build-tools dirs aren't readable.

Needs a resolver that locates the SDK via $ANDROID_HOME, $ANDROID_SDK_ROOT, or the default macOS path ~/Library/Android/sdk; returns the SDK root in AdditionalReadDirs and the env var in ResolvedEnv.

Key paths and env vars:
- read_dirs (manifest): ~/.android (avd, keystore, cache), ~/.gradle/caches/transforms (already partly covered by java-gradle's ~/.gradle if it exists), ~/Library/Android (parent of sdk)
- read_dirs (resolver): $ANDROID_HOME / $ANDROID_SDK_ROOT / ~/Library/Android/sdk
- env_passthrough: ANDROID_HOME, ANDROID_SDK_ROOT, ANDROID_NDK_HOME, GRADLE_USER_HOME (all need adding to safeEnvKeys — path pointers, no creds)
- detect: settings.gradle OR settings.gradle.kts with an :app or :android subproject pattern is the cleanest signal; simpler heuristic: build.gradle(.kts) AND any *.kt file under app/src — but hazmat detect is file-list-based per integration_manifest.go, so a pragmatic detect is 'local.properties' (Android-specific) OR 'app/build.gradle' OR 'app/build.gradle.kts'

Coexistence with java-gradle: this integration should LAYER on top of java-gradle (both active when Android), not replace it. Decision needed in design: does android-gradle subsume java-gradle for these projects, or do they merge? Recommend merge (java-gradle provides JDK paths; android-gradle adds SDK paths). 

- backup excludes: build/, .gradle/, .cxx/, captures/, local.properties, *.iml, .idea/
acceptance_criteria: 1) hazmat/integrations/android-gradle.yaml exists, validates. 2) Resolver locates the SDK and returns root + env in ResolvedEnv. 3) ANDROID_HOME / ANDROID_SDK_ROOT / ANDROID_NDK_HOME / GRADLE_USER_HOME added to safeEnvKeys. 4) Detection coexists with java-gradle (both activate on an Android project — confirm via test). 5) Test in integration_resolver_test.go. 6) End-to-end DEFERRED: a real Android assembleDebug needs an actual Android project + emulator — write a unit test that asserts the SDK platforms/build-tools paths are in the resolved read_dirs against a fake SDK fixture, and document the manual smoke-test command in docs/integrations.md.
notes: Android assembleDebug end-to-end is heavyweight — for CI coverage rely on the unit test against a fake SDK layout. The integration's failure mode is identical to python-uv's earlier bug: ancestor metadata grants on ~/Library/Android missing because read_dir wasn't declared. Verify with hazmat explain showing the SDK root in Auto read-only.
close_reason: android-gradle integration shipped. Three unit tests: SDK probe success with fake SDK, SDK probe failure when candidate lacks platforms/, java-gradle coexistence on Android project. End-to-end assembleDebug remains deferred per acceptance criteria (needs real Android project + emulator); manual command documented in docs/integrations.md.

title: integration: bun (runtime + package manager)
description:
Bun at ~16% of JS runtime users (SoJS 2024) and the runtime Claude Code itself is built on (Pragmatic Engineer 2024 piece on Anthropic's stack). Bun installs under ~/.bun (binary + cache + global packages) and runs 'bun install' against a global cache there.

Needs a small resolver because the bun binary is found wherever brew or the official curl installer placed it — typically /opt/homebrew/bin/bun (Homebrew) or ~/.bun/bin/bun (curl install). The resolver should probe 'bun --revision' to confirm presence and then expose ~/.bun (manifest) plus any non-Homebrew install prefix.

Key paths and env vars:
- read_dirs (manifest): ~/.bun
- read_dirs (resolver): bun install prefix when not Homebrew (otherwise covered by base /opt/homebrew)
- env_passthrough: BUN_INSTALL (add to safeEnvKeys)
- detect: bun.lockb OR bunfig.toml
- backup excludes: node_modules/, .next/, .nuxt/, dist/, out/

Coexistence: bun projects often also have package.json — the 'node' integration would fire too. Both should activate; backup excludes dedup. Bun does NOT use ~/.local/share/pnpm or ~/.npm — separate store.
acceptance_criteria: 1) hazmat/integrations/bun.yaml exists, validates. 2) Resolver entry in integration_resolver.go that probes 'bun --revision'; on success returns ~/.bun (resolved) in AdditionalReadDirs and BUN_INSTALL in ResolvedEnv. 3) Test in integration_resolver_test.go. 4) BUN_INSTALL added to safeEnvKeys. 5) Detection fires on bun.lockb. 6) End-to-end: 'hazmat exec -- bun install' on a tiny package.json+bun.lockb fixture succeeds, no denials. 7) Coexistence test: project with both package.json and bun.lockb activates 'node' AND 'bun'.
notes: Bun's binary signature on macOS occasionally trips AMFI on first run — confirm the AMFI denials in hazmat-debug log are absent after the integration is active. Reference the 2026-04-22 SBPL debug memory for log show predicate format.
close_reason: bun integration shipped. Resolver covers LookPath probe + Homebrew fallback paths; verified by unit test. End-to-end: bun install + bun -e require lodash succeeds inside hazmat exec.

title: Avoid double hashing in harness asset sync planning
description: Reduce redundant work in managed harness asset sync. The native-launch path currently computes a preview diff and then recomputes desired state and fingerprints again when applying the sync. Preserve the current safety checks while avoiding duplicate hashing where possible so larger managed asset trees do not scale poorly.
acceptance_criteria: Harness asset sync no longer re-hashes the same desired tree twice per launch in the common path, or has an equivalent cheaper change detector; behavior and warnings stay unchanged; tests cover the revised planning/apply flow.
notes: Revisited while implementing sandboxing-1zrp.3. The obvious optimization is to reuse preview desired-state data during apply, but that can leave stale fingerprints or incorrect adopt decisions if host assets change between planning and execution. Leaving this open for a correctness-preserving design instead of forcing a risky shortcut.
close_reason: Preview now carries desired harness-asset state plus source metadata snapshots, and apply reuses it on the common path while falling back to a fresh collect when sources change; added reuse/fallback tests and reran go test ./...

title: codex: support 'hazmat codex app' (Codex desktop GUI under containment) [stretch]
description:
Codex CLI exposes 'codex app' which launches the Codex desktop application — downloads the macOS .app installer if missing, then runs the GUI client. Today this almost certainly will not work under hazmat containment.

Likely blockers (not yet root-caused, just enumerated from the GUI surface area):
  - WindowServer access: mach-lookup com.apple.windowserver.active and friends — required for any AppKit/SwiftUI window creation. The agent user is not logged into a GUI session.
  - App bundle install path: codex downloads the .app bundle (likely to /Applications or ~/Applications). /Applications is system-owned; the agent cannot write there. ~/Applications under the agent home would work for installation but the launchd mechanisms that register apps may not.
  - Login session prerequisites: macOS GUI apps assume a Window Server session token that the agent (which has no GUI login) doesn't have. May surface as crashes deep in CFBundle/AppKit init.
  - Codec / codex_apps MCP: the in-process MCP that talks to chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/apps was already observed failing with a network/initialize error during the headless 'hazmat codex' work today (2026-04-22). The app variant probably exercises the same path more aggressively.
  - Sandbox-on-sandbox: codex's app may invoke its own seatbelt or App Sandbox profile that conflicts with hazmat's.

Open question: whether running a GUI desktop app under a non-GUI agent user is even meaningful. Two viable framings:
  1. 'Run codex app under containment' — non-trivial; needs WindowServer surface, .app install handling, and probably a launchd login session for the agent.
  2. 'Detect 'codex app' and proxy/launch it on the host instead' — passes the request through to host-side codex while keeping every other 'hazmat codex …' invocation contained. Lower complexity; preserves containment for code-paths that matter.

Triage before commit: spike to confirm what fails first, then choose framing 1 or 2. Stretch goal — main 'hazmat codex' (chat) is fully working as of commit eaaaa1c.
design:
Likely needs a proper bootstrap step (e.g. 'hazmat bootstrap codex-app' or extending bootstrap_codex.go) rather than relying on 'codex app' to download+install on first run inside the sandbox. The bootstrap would:
  - Download the Codex .app bundle (the same one 'codex app' fetches) and install it to /Users/agent/Applications/
  - Set perms so the agent can launch it
  - Persist version state (similar to recordHarnessInstalled for the CLI today)
  - Pre-create any cache/config dirs the .app expects (analogous to the .codex/.agents shared-dir steps)

Then 'hazmat codex app' becomes 'launch already-installed app under containment' rather than 'install + launch in one shot'. This separates the install-time decisions (which run with normal host network/perms) from the runtime sandbox decisions (which need the GUI/WindowServer surface). Same shape as the existing CLI bootstrap split.
acceptance_criteria: 'hazmat codex app' produces a usable Codex desktop experience for the user, OR cleanly errors out with a documented reason if the chosen framing is to disallow it. Either way: predictable, never silently hangs or leaks.
notes:
Filed during the codex unblocking session on 2026-04-22 as a stretch goal. Depends on the broader per-harness seatbelt scoping work (sandboxing-m7f7) so the GUI surface doesn't bleed into claude/opencode policies.
Research note docs/research/2026-05-28-codex-ui-app-sandboxing.md narrows this full-GUI item to a stretch path. Recommended order is first contained `codex app-server` backend (sandboxing-txz6), then stock app external app-server/remote-environment attach probe (sandboxing-lsn2). Full GUI launch as `agent` should wait until those paths are proven insufficient because the GUI path likely needs WindowServer/LaunchServices/TCC/keychain/Electron lifecycle and TLA+ model work.
close_reason: Implemented a fail-fast guard for hazmat codex app with docs and unit coverage; full GUI launch remains unsupported while app-server/attach paths are the modeled integration routes.

title: hazmat-launch: 'exec' subprocesses leak when invoked outside a TTY
description:
Observed 2026-04-22 while trying to non-interactively smoke-test 'hazmat codex --version' from a non-TTY shell:

1. The hazmat-launch process spawned by sudo never exits.
2. The agent-side child (test -x, /bin/zsh -lc 'exec codex …') burns CPU at ~70% indefinitely.
3. log show shows no sandbox denials for that PID — it's stuck in a tight wake loop (kernel logged: 'caught waking the CPU 45001 times over 33 seconds, averaging 1324 wakes/second').
4. Killing requires 'sudo -u agent /bin/kill -9 <pid>'.
5. Same pattern observed for go test runs that exercise hazmat-launch in subprocess form: TestExecModeBypassesPolicyValidation and TestCloseInheritedFDs_ClosesExtraFiles processes leaked from earlier 'go test' runs (PIDs 3934, 5822, 58173, 58605) had been spinning for 30-60 minutes.

Likely root cause: hazmat-launch / sandbox_init or the wrapped /bin/zsh -lc launcher waits on a TTY/pty interaction that never arrives when stdin is not a tty, instead of detecting non-tty and either erroring out or running through.

Reproduction: 'hazmat codex --version 2>&1 | tail' from a context where stdin is not a tty — the parent will appear to hang and a child sudo+hazmat-launch will spin forever even after the parent shell is killed.

Workaround: only invoke hazmat harness commands from a real TTY; clean up any leaked PIDs via 'sudo -u agent kill'.
acceptance_criteria: hazmat codex --version (or any 'hazmat <harness>' command) invoked from a non-TTY context exits within a reasonable time (a few seconds for --version) and does not leave orphaned hazmat-launch / agent processes consuming CPU.
close_reason: Fixed in <commit-hash>. Root cause: closeInheritedFDs iterated 3..RLIMIT_NOFILE which is RLIM_INFINITY (~9 quintillion) under 'ulimit -n unlimited'. Switched to /dev/fd enumeration. Verified 'hazmat codex exec' from a non-TTY shell completes round-trip in seconds.

title: config import: self-heal when agent file ownership/perms are wrong
description:
scanCodexAuthFile / scanOpenCodeAuthFile / scanClaudeCredentialFile only compare bytes when deciding 'unchanged'. They don't check that the agent file is owned by the agent at the right perms. After landing the writeMaybePrivilegedFile ownership fix, a previously-broken on-disk file (host-owned 0600) won't be re-imported because content matches → status=unchanged → no rewrite. User has to manually 'sudo -u agent rm' the bad file before re-running import.

Fix: extend the auth-file scan to inspect ownership/perms and mark as 'needs re-import' (status=conflict or new) if owner != agent or mode != expected, regardless of content equality. Apply to all three (claude / codex / opencode).
acceptance_criteria: Given an agent auth file owned by the host user (mode 0600), 'hazmat config import <harness>' detects the bad ownership and re-writes the file via the agent path without manual sudo cleanup.
close_reason: Landed in this commit. agentOwnsFile helper in agent_user.go (var-exposed for test stubbing); all four scan paths (claude/codex/opencode/gemini) demote 'unchanged' to 'new' when content matches but agent doesn't own the file, so the apply path rewrites via the agent-write code path. Closes the manual cleanup gap from the pre-6a466e7 broken-ownership state. Tests cover both branches.

title: gemini: env-var path (GEMINI_API_KEY / GOOGLE_API_KEY / Vertex flags) in 'hazmat config agent'
description:
Extend 'hazmat config agent' to support the gemini env-var paths analogous to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY:
  - GEMINI_API_KEY (AI Studio)
  - GOOGLE_API_KEY + GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true (Vertex)
  - GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT (paid Code Assist)
Decide whether to keep prompting one-at-a-time or to make this harness-aware (see sandboxing-ofac). Likely simplest: when bootstrapSelection=gemini, prompt for whichever env var is set in the host environment, mirror to agent's .zshrc.
acceptance_criteria: With GEMINI_API_KEY set in host env, 'hazmat config agent' offers to seed it into /Users/agent/.zshrc; verified by 'env | grep GEMINI' inside 'hazmat shell'.
close_reason: Landed in 48fce7e. config_agent.go now iterates harnessAPIKeyPrompts table per installed harness; gemini gets a GEMINI_API_KEY prompt with paste/host-env/skip flow. title: Docs: explain shared-daemon workflow (niche-sieve/docker-infra pattern)
description:
Document the 'code-only contained session against externally managed local services' workflow for projects that depend on the shared host Docker daemon. This is the recommended pattern for repos like niche-sieve/docker-infra.

Core model: Hazmat contains the agent away from the host user and Docker control plane. The normal-user terminal owns the shared Docker world. Docker is outside hazmat, code is inside.

Document these specifics:
1. Workflow: Terminal 1 runs docker-infra + project services normally. Terminal 2 runs hazmat claude --ignore-docker (future: --docker=none) for code-only sessions.
2. The agent uses host-published ports (localhost:5433, localhost:6380, localhost:8000), NOT Docker service names (postgres, shared-postgres, api).
3. Seatbelt grants full read/write to the project dir AND broad read/write to /Users/agent, with credential paths denied last (session.go:1210). Not just project dir.
4. localhost is inside the blast radius. pf is a soft blocklist that otherwise says 'pass out quick user agent' (init.go:19). Agent can talk to any host-published service on unblocked ports.
5. Hot-reload is not uniform: API/frontend hot-reload via Compose watch, but worker needs manual docker restart because auto-restart crashes running Prefect flows (docker-compose.dev.yml:54).
6. Indirect mutation via mounted source: agent edits become running code inside containers via Compose watch. Containment boundary for running services is 'whatever the agent can write to mounted source paths.'
7. Residual risk: Traefik dashboard, ngrok dashboard, debug endpoints, broad DB creds, destructive internal APIs — all reachable if exposed on unblocked ports. For stronger dev-environment containment, next step is Tier 4 (full VM).
8. Operational hardening: expose only needed ports, use disposable dev data, use low-privilege local DB/API creds, keep sibling repos read-only (-R), stop admin surfaces when not needed.

This is not a hack — it is a valid workflow. The docs should frame it that way.
design: Add section to docs/tier3-docker-sandboxes.md or a new docs/shared-daemon-projects.md. Reference the scope decision. Include example workflow: hazmat config docker none -C ~/workspace/niche-sieve, then hazmat claude -C ~/workspace/niche-sieve works without blocking. User runs docker compose in a separate terminal. Cross-reference from overview.md tier selection table.
